name: Nunchuk
purpose: Multisignature and miniscript wallet for individuals and groups (Qt 6 desktop client built on libnunchuk), with optional paid assisted-wallet, inheritance and collaborative-custody services from Nunchuk. It connects to Electrum servers (Nunchuk's own by default) or to a Bitcoin Core node over RPC; signers are hardware wallets over USB (bundled HWI), QR or files, plus software keys.

maintenance.evidence: 2.9.1 released in October 2026 (release page: published 9 October from commit 0341ebd; feed entry updated 2026-10-10), 2.9.0 2026-10-08 (Qt 5 to Qt 6, hardware device as inheritance key), 2.6.0 to 2.6.6 between 2026-06-22 and 2026-08-21, 2.5.0 2026-05-21. Latest commits 2026-10-14 (Taproot Ledger fallback, PR #131).

platforms.windowsDistribution: nunchuk-windows-v2.9.1-x64-setup.exe: Inno Setup installer with PrivilegesRequired=admin, DefaultDirName {autopf}\Nunchuk (Program Files), ArchitecturesAllowed x64compatible; upstream's smoke test installs with /VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART /NOCANCEL /SP- /NOICONS /TASKS= and uninstalls with /VERYSILENT /NORESTART. nunchuk-windows-v2.9.1-x64-portable.zip: deterministic uncompressed ZIP with nunchuk-qt.exe, hwi.exe, qt6keychain.dll, build-info.json, Qt 6.9.3, OpenSSL 3.5.7 and MSVC runtime DLLs (no installer, no elevation). The build workflow states that Windows release artefacts are unsigned (no Authenticode). A separate workflow publishes SHA256SUMS and SHA256SUMS.asc.
platforms.other: macOS .dmg (arm64 and x86_64), Linux AppImage (x86_64 and aarch64; reproducible builds independently verifiable for Linux only), iOS and Android apps (separate projects).

interfaces.description: Qt 6/QML desktop client (nunchuk-qt.exe); settings for Electrum servers, Bitcoin Core RPC, Tor proxy, HWI path, database encryption, fees and currency.
interfaces.authentication: Optional Nunchuk account sign-in for subscription and group features

interfaces.description: libnunchuk Electrum client: server string "ssl://host:port" for TLS, anything else plain TCP (default port 50001); server.version("Nunchuk", ["1.3", "1.4.2"]); request batching for ElectrumX, electrs and Fulcrum. Default servers: mainnet.nunchuk.io:51001 (Nunchuk-operated), testnet.nunchuk.io:50001, ssl://mempool.space:60602 for signet; optional dual-server mode. TLS: with a pinned certificateFile the chain and host identity are checked; without it self-signed certificates are accepted with a warning; .onion hosts are not verified.

Optional Bitcoin Core RPC back end (settings enableCoreRPC, coreRPCAddress, coreRPCPort, coreRPCName, coreRPCPassword): creates and loads a Core wallet named nunchuk (createwallet nunchuk true true "" false, a descriptor wallet on Core 23+ by default), imports descriptors with importdescriptors (importmulti below 23.0) and uses getnetworkinfo, getblockchaininfo, getwalletinfo, getaddressinfo, listunspent, listtransactions, gettransaction, rescanblockchain, estimatesmartfee, getmempoolinfo and sendrawtransaction.
interfaces.authentication: HTTP basic authentication with RPC user and password only; no cookie support

interfaces.description: USB hardware wallets through the bundled hwi.exe (setting hwiPath, default "hwi"; a custom HWI can be enabled with enableCustomizeHWIDriver). The Windows build pins hwi-3.2.4 from github.com/nogibi/HWI (a patched HWI whose releases add registerdescriptor, miniscript and MuSig2 descriptor parsing), not an upstream bitcoin-core/HWI release.
interfaces.authentication: On-device confirmation

interfaces.description: QR scanning (zxing-cpp) and display for air-gapped signers; nunchuk.io lists Keystone, Foundation Passport, SeedSigner, Krux, Jade and others. The QR encodings used on desktop were not verified.
PSBT files and wallet configuration export as output descriptors or BSMS (BIP129); microSD workflows for air-gapped signers such as Coldcard.
Nunchuk account services (assisted wallets, inheritance plans, group wallets) over HTTPS and a Matrix-based messaging layer (libQuotient submodule).
interfaces.authentication: Nunchuk account

cli: None: nunchuk-qt.exe parses no command-line arguments (main.cpp marks argc/argv unused). The Inno Setup installer accepts the standard switches (/VERYSILENT, /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES, /NORESTART, /SP-, /DIR=, /TASKS=).
remoteManagement: None. Collaborative and assisted features are coordinated through Nunchuk's servers with an account.
nodeCompatibility: Electrum servers: Fulcrum, electrs and ElectrumX (TLS with the ssl:// prefix; pin a self-signed certificate with certificateFile). Bitcoin Core RPC: descriptor wallets and importdescriptors on Core >= 23, so the code path is compatible with Core 30.x and 31.1 (no removed RPCs used); needs server=1, wallets enabled and an rpcuser/rpcpassword or rpcauth user (no cookie). The wallet 'nunchuk' is created without load_on_startup, so on a pruned node it can fall behind pruning while Nunchuk is closed; rescanblockchain cannot reach below the prune height. Bitcoin Knots >= 29.4.1 follows a different chain.

dependencies.notes: An Electrum server (Nunchuk's public server by default) or a Bitcoin Core RPC endpoint with a dedicated rpcauth user.
Bundled hwi.exe from a patched fork (nogibi/HWI 3.2.4 in the Windows build); replaceable through the hwiPath setting.
enableTorProxy with torProxyAddress 127.0.0.1 and torProxyPort 9050 (SOCKS5, optional username and password).
Devices listed on nunchuk.io; TAPSIGNER is primarily an NFC workflow on mobile.

networking: No listening ports. Outbound: the Electrum server (default mainnet.nunchuk.io:51001), optionally Bitcoin Core RPC (127.0.0.1:8332 by default), Nunchuk APIs and messaging for accounts, and mempool.space links for transactions (https://mempool.space/tx/, /testnet4/tx/, /signet/tx/). Optional SOCKS5 proxy (Tor) for Electrum connections.
storage: Settings in the Windows registry: QSettings NativeFormat, user scope, organisation 'nunchuk', application 'NunchukClient' (HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\nunchuk\NunchukClient). Keys are stored unprefixed for guests and as <group>/<key> when a group is set; primaryServer, isStarted and mainnetList are always unprefixed. The mainnet server key is spelt mainnestServer. Wallet data under QStandardPaths::AppDataLocation (expected %APPDATA%\nunchuk\NunchukClient); optional database encryption (enableDBEncryption, default false). In Bitcoin Core: one watch-only wallet named nunchuk.
resources: Not documented. Qt 6 including Qt WebEngine (Chromium) in the bundle.
security: The default Electrum server is operated by Nunchuk and learns the wallet's addresses: point Nunchuk at the user's own server. Nunchuk can create software keys (stored by the app; database encryption is off by default): BTCortex must not collect, back up or transmit them. Paid assisted, inheritance and group features involve Nunchuk-operated services and an account (key arrangements per plan not verified). Windows binaries are not Authenticode-signed; SHA256SUMS.asc is produced by a CI workflow with a key held as a GitHub secret (release notes link key 8C8ECD3F660CA53CD878792A6E38A462ED2EF525 on keys.openpgp.org); Windows and macOS reproducible builds are not yet independently verifiable. The bundled HWI comes from a non-upstream fork. Core RPC credentials are stored in the registry. Unpinned self-signed Electrum certificates are accepted with a warning.
licenceNotes: The README states GNU GPL v3 (libnunchuk is GPL v3 as well); whether -only or -or-later applies was not checked. Redistribution requires offering the source. Nunchuk's subscription services have their own terms.
integrationMechanisms: Download nunchuk-windows-v<v>-x64-portable.zip (preferred: no elevation) or the Inno Setup installer together with SHA256SUMS and SHA256SUMS.asc; verify the signature against the published key (8C8ECD3F660CA53CD878792A6E38A462ED2EF525, to be confirmed) and the SHA-256
Installer route: run the setup with /VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART /SP- from an elevated context (PrivilegesRequired=admin)
Launch nunchuk-qt.exe (no command-line options)

Guided configuration: show the Electrum endpoint (ssl://127.0.0.1:50002 plus the server certificate file for pinning) or a dedicated rpcauth user and password for the managed node; writing HKCU\Software\nunchuk\NunchukClient values (mainnestServer, enableCoreRPC, coreRPCAddress, coreRPCPort, coreRPCName, coreRPCPassword, enableTorProxy, torProxyAddress, torProxyPort, certificateFile, enableCertificateFile) while the app is closed is technically possible but relies on undocumented, group-prefixed registry keys
Create a dedicated rpcauth user for Nunchuk and keep its Core wallet 'nunchuk' loaded at node start (wallet=nunchuk) on pruned nodes
Detect: HKCU\Software\nunchuk\NunchukClient, the Program Files\Nunchuk installation, nunchuk-qt.exe processes

feasibility.notes: The portable ZIP allows a per-user install without elevation, and checksums are signed. Pre-configuration is the weak point: settings live in the registry under undocumented keys that move under a group prefix once the user signs in, Core RPC needs a password (no cookie), and the default server is Nunchuk's own. BTCortex should install, verify and launch Nunchuk and present the connection values for the user to enter; registry pre-seeding stays research-only until tested. Priority P2.

notes: Nunchuk announced generalised miniscript on 2025-08-27: native SegWit miniscript with Coldcard, TAPSIGNER, Jade, Ledger and Specter DIY; Taproot miniscript with Coldcard, Ledger and Specter DIY; MuSig2 with software keys. libnunchuk contains a miniscript module; how much of this the desktop UI exposes was not verified. Wallet configurations export as output descriptors or BSMS. BIP329 label support was not found. Assisted wallets, inheritance plans and group wallets require a Nunchuk account and subscription (plans for individuals, families and groups, and advisors are listed on nunchuk.io).

platforms.windowsDistribution: Bitcoin-Safe-2.1.3-setup.exe (NSIS: RequestExecutionLevel admin, default folder $PROGRAMFILES64\<product>, Add/Remove Programs entry and a bitcoin: URI handler under HKCU, desktop and Start Menu shortcuts including a 'Testnet' shortcut; the uninstaller removes only the program folder) and Bitcoin-Safe-2.1.3-portable.exe (single executable, no installer). Windows binaries are Authenticode-signed through SignPath with a certificate issued by the SignPath Foundation and are reproducible (built under Wine in Docker).
platforms.other: macOS arm64 .dmg; Linux x86_64 AppImage (tar.gz) and .deb; Flatpak (reproducible Docker build); from source with Poetry (Python >= 3.10, < 3.14).

interfaces.description: PyQt6 desktop GUI; on mainnet it enforces hardware-only seeds (no seed generation or storage), so it works as a watch-only coordinator with external signers.
interfaces.authentication: Optional app-lock password (verifier derived with 600 000 iterations).

interfaces.description: USB hardware signers through the bitcoin-usb library, which depends on HWI (hwi >= 3.2.0 on main). Listed signers: Coldcard Q, Mk4 and Mk5, BitBox02 and BitBox02 Nova, Foundation Passport (Core, Prime), Jade and Jade Plus, Trezor Safe 3, 5 and 7, Keystone, Ledger Nano S, S Plus, X and Flex, Specter DIY / Shield / Shield Lite, SeedSigner, Krux and MetroVault (each over USB, QR or SD card as the device allows).
interfaces.authentication: PIN and passphrase entered on the device.

interfaces.description: Animated QR codes in UR and Coldcard BBQr formats, with laptop-camera scanning (bitcoin-qr-tools), for descriptors, PSBTs and message signing.

PSBT, transaction and wallet files (open from the command line or by drag and drop), microSD workflows, BIP329 label import and export (and Electrum label import), CSV import and export, PDF backup sheets that include the descriptor. Configuration in bitcoin_safe.conf (JSON) under the per-user config directory, wallets in per-network subfolders.

Default backend: BIP157/158 compact block filters through the Kyoto module for BDK, downloading filters from random Bitcoin Core peers (cbf_connections default 2) or from configured peers such as the user's own node at 127.0.0.1:8333; a separate P2P listener (default 'automatic', 4 parallel connections on mainnet) gives instant notifications for unconfirmed transactions.
Optional Electrum backend (electrum_url, electrum_use_ssl); mainnet default electrum.blockstream.info:50002 over SSL.
Optional Esplora HTTP backend (esplora_url; no mainnet default).

A Bitcoin Core RPC backend type exists in the network configuration (BlockchainType.RPC with rpc_ip 127.0.0.1, rpc_port 8332 on mainnet, rpc_username, rpc_password); the privacy policy mentions an 'RPC server' in Network settings.
interfaces.authentication: RPC user name and password (no cookie option found in the configuration class).

interfaces.description: Sync & Chat plugin: encrypted wallet chat, PSBT sharing and label synchronisation between trusted devices over Nostr relays (default relays or user-specified).
interfaces.authentication: Device keys exchanged between trusted devices.

cli: Bitcoin-Safe executable: --network <name> (lower-case bdk.Network names such as bitcoin, testnet, testnet4, signet, regtest; invalid values are logged and ignored), --profile, --trace-startup-windows, and positional FILE ... (tx, psbt or wallet files to open at start-up). Unknown arguments are logged and ignored; there are no data-directory, portable-mode or version flags on main.
remoteManagement: None; desktop GUI only. The Sync & Chat collaboration features use Nostr relays and are not a management API.
nodeCompatibility: Uses no Bitcoin Core wallet RPCs (BDK keeps its own wallet), so the Core 30 removal of legacy wallets does not affect it (inference). Own Bitcoin Core node as a compact-filter peer: the node must build and serve filters (blockfilterindex=1, peerblockfilters=1) and accept P2P connections (listen=1; for BTCortex bind=127.0.0.1). A pruned node advertises NODE_NETWORK_LIMITED and serves only recent blocks (BIP159), so blocks for older filter matches would have to come from additional peers (peer_selection_mode 'additional' is the default; 'only_configured' would restrict it) - not tested. Electrum servers (fulcrum, electrs) and Esplora work as alternatives but need an unpruned node. The RPC backend type exists in code; its availability in the 2.1.3 UI and its behaviour on a pruned node were not verified.

dependencies.notes: As a compact-filter peer (blockfilterindex=1, peerblockfilters=1, P2P listening on loopback) or through the RPC backend type.
Electrum backend alternative to compact block filters; requires an unpruned node.
Pulled in through bitcoin-usb (hwi >= 3.2.0); no separate HWI installation is needed.
Hardware signers over USB, QR or microSD depending on the device; required on mainnet because the wallet refuses software seeds there.
Not bundled; a SOCKS proxy can be set per network (proxy_url); a Tor onion URL is offered for the mempool.space fee data.

networking: Outbound only: Bitcoin P2P port 8333 (mainnet) to two compact-filter peers by default plus the transaction-notification listener; mempool.space for fee data (onion alternative available); electrum.blockstream.info:50002 or an Esplora URL when those backends are selected; Nostr relays only when Sync & Chat is enabled; update notifications with automatic signature verification. An optional proxy (proxy_url) applies per network. No inbound ports.
storage: Not documented. Configuration and wallet files are small; compact-filter headers and filters are cached locally (size not documented).
resources: Not documented. Initial compact-filter synchronisation of a new or restored wallet usually takes 5 to 30 minutes; an already synchronised wallet catches up in under 30 seconds (project documentation).
security: Mainnet enforces hardware-only seeds, which fits BTCortex's rule of never handling mnemonics. Releases are signed with the OpenPGP key 2759 AA71 4856 8ECC B03B 7630 1D82 124B 440F 612D (published on keys.openpgp.org, which shows no identity for it); Windows binaries are Authenticode-signed through the SignPath Foundation; builds are reproducible (Windows hashes match after stripping the Authenticode signature with osslsigncode). The app verifies update signatures itself. Privacy: the code-signing policy says the default blockchain data comes from Blockstream's Electrum/Esplora servers, while the README and network configuration make compact block filters the default where available; fee data comes from mempool.space; Sync & Chat exposes encrypted traffic metadata to Nostr relays. Address-poisoning detection warns about look-alike addresses. The uninstaller does not delete user data.
licenceNotes: GPL-3.0-only (pyproject.toml). Redistribution requires offering the corresponding source; downloading the official artefacts at install time avoids bundling.
integrationMechanisms: Download Bitcoin-Safe-<version>-portable.exe (or -setup.exe) and its .asc from the GitHub release; verify the OpenPGP signature against the pinned fingerprint 2759AA7148568ECCB03B76301D82124B440F612D, optionally also the Authenticode signature

Zero-touch install without elevation: place the portable executable in a versioned per-user directory under %LOCALAPPDATA% and create BTCortex-owned shortcuts; the NSIS installer requires administrator rights and its script does not handle /S explicitly (standard NSIS silent mode untested)
Launch with --network <name> and, for PSBT hand-over, the path of a .psbt file as a positional argument

Pre-configure the backend only while the app is closed, by editing network_configs in bitcoin_safe.conf (JSON; on Windows expected at %LOCALAPPDATA%\bitcoin_safe\bitcoin_safe\ via appdirs) - server_type, electrum_url/electrum_use_ssl, configured_peers, peer_selection_mode, proxy_url - preserving unknown fields; validate against each release before enabling
Prepare the managed node when it should serve as compact-filter peer: blockfilterindex=1, peerblockfilters=1, listen=1 with bind=127.0.0.1
Detect existing installations through the HKCU uninstall entry and the bitcoin: URI handler written by the NSIS installer

feasibility.notes: Signed, reproducible x64 portable executable that BTCortex can install and update per user, and sensible defaults (compact block filters from random peers) that work with a pruned local node and without any configuration. Backend pre-configuration is possible but only from the source code (JSON with migration code, no published schema), so it needs per-release validation; full management is therefore not recommended yet. P2: a strong hardware-signer coordinator that complements Sparrow, but not one of the essential Phase 5 integrations.

notes: Powered by BDK; the compact-filter client is the Kyoto module for BDK. Multisig with step-by-step setup, PDF backup sheets and test transactions; collaboration and label sync over Nostr; money-flow diagrams; RBF and CPFP; CSV export. Miniscript and Taproot multisig are not documented. The supported-signer list includes Trezor Safe 7, Coldcard Mk5 and MetroVault, which are newer than most third-party compatibility tables. Bitcoin-Safe's audit badge links to WalletScrutiny; no formal security audit is described.

unverifiedClaims: The owner identity of OpenPGP key 2759AA7148568ECCB03B76301D82124B440F612D is not shown on keys.openpgp.org or on the verification page.
The Windows configuration path %LOCALAPPDATA%\bitcoin_safe\bitcoin_safe\bitcoin_safe.conf is inferred from appdirs.user_config_dir('bitcoin_safe') semantics, not observed on a Windows machine.
Whether the portable executable stores its configuration in the same per-user directory as the installed version was not verified.
Silent installation of the NSIS setup.exe with /S was not tested.
Supported Windows versions are not documented.
Availability of the RPC backend in the 2.1.3 user interface, the proxy URL format and the behaviour of the compact-filter client against a pruned local node were not verified.
The installer's 'Testnet' shortcut passes --testnet, which __main__.py on main does not define (it would be ignored); whether released builds handle it differently was not checked.

name: Wasabi Wallet
purpose: Open-source, privacy-focused single-signature Bitcoin desktop wallet with a built-in WabiSabi CoinJoin client, bundled Tor and client-side BIP157/BIP158 compact-block-filter synchronisation. It can use the user's own Bitcoin Core node over JSON-RPC for filters, blocks, fee estimates and broadcasting.

maintenance.evidence: Wasabi Wallet v2.8.4 published 2026-10-13 (v2.8.3 2026-09-14, v2.8.0 2026-06-27, v2.7.0 2025-08-30). Latest master commit 2026-10-21 ('Remove Indexer (#15190)', author lontivero). Repository WalletWasabi/WalletWasabi is not archived. zkSNACKs Ltd., the original developer, discontinued its default CoinJoin coordinator on 2024-06-01 and the repository moved from zkSNACKs to the self-named WalletWasabi organisation with v2.0.8 (2024-06-01). Development has continued since: releases are published by the WalletWasabi organisation and the Windows MSI is Authenticode-signed by maintainer Lucas Ontivero.

platforms.windowsVersions: Windows 10 1607 or later and Windows 11 23H2 or later (2.8.4 release notes)
platforms.windowsDistribution: Wasabi-2.8.4.msi (99 340 288 bytes; WiX, InstallScope perMachine, Platform x64, default folder C:\Program Files\WasabiWallet\, Authenticode signer shown as Lucas Ontivero; MajorUpgrade blocks downgrades; UpgradeCode {D8E80773-D8CF-4031-B8B3-AA750AF0B413}) and Wasabi-2.8.4-win-x64.zip (96 203 518 bytes, self-contained, no installer). Every file has a detached .asc signature; SHA256SUMS, SHA256SUMS.asc and SHA256SUMS.wasabisig cover the set. Executables: wassabee.exe (GUI) and wassabeed.exe (headless daemon). The website links only the MSI for Windows. No Windows arm64 build (arm64 exists for macOS and Linux only).
platforms.other: macOS 14 or later (x64 and arm64 .dmg and .zip); Linux x64 and arm64 (.deb, .AppImage, .tar.gz, .zip; Ubuntu 22.04+, Fedora 42+, Debian 12+; Tails and Whonix detected automatically since 2.8.0); Nix flake in the repository. No mobile apps.

interfaces.description: Avalonia desktop GUI (wassabee.exe). Settings > Bitcoin > 'Connect to Bitcoin Node RPC' holds the node endpoint and credential string; Settings > Coordinator holds the coordinator connection string; a status-bar icon shows the Bitcoin RPC state.
interfaces.authentication: Per-wallet password (applied as the BIP39 passphrase).

interfaces.description: Optional JSON-RPC server: JsonRpcServerEnabled (false on mainnet, true on testnet/regtest/signet by default), JsonRpcServerPrefixes http://127.0.0.1:37128/ and http://localhost:37128/; wallet calls use the path /<WalletName>. Methods: getstatus, createwallet, recoverwallet, listwallets, loadwallet, listcoins, listunspentcoins, getwalletinfo, getnewaddress, send, build, broadcast, speeduptransaction, canceltransaction, gethistory, getfeerates, listkeys, excludefromcoinjoin, startcoinjoin, payincoinjoin, listpaymentsincoinjoin, cancelpaymentincoinjoin, startcoinjoinsweep, stopcoinjoin, buildunsafetransaction, stop. No TLS, no batching, requests processed serially; optional onion service with --rpconionenabled (new onion address at every start).
interfaces.authentication: HTTP authentication with JsonRpcUser and JsonRpcPassword (random 12-character defaults generated when the default configuration is created); anonymous access is refused. 2.8.4 hardened JSON-RPC authentication (#15134).

interfaces.description: Startup parameters for wassabee.exe and wassabeed.exe in the form --switch=value (case-insensitive) or environment variables WASABI_<SWITCH>. Precedence: command line, then environment, then Config.json. Overrides are not written back to Config.json.

Per-network JSON configuration in %APPDATA%\WalletWasabi\Client: Config.json (mainnet), Config.TestNet.json (testnet4), Config.RegTest.json and Config.Signet.json, all with ConfigVersion 4 since 2.8.0. The folder also holds UIConfig.json, the Wallets folder, a 'network' file naming the last network and a '.wasabi-lock' file that is held exclusively while an instance runs. An unreadable config makes Wasabi write Config.Default.json next to it and stop with an error.

USB hardware wallets through the bundled HWI binary (Wasabi does not need a separately installed HWI). Documented as tested with Trezor Model T, Ledger Nano S, S Plus and X and Coldcard; the website also names Blockstream Jade and BitBox02 (BitBox02-BtcOnly since 2.0.7, BitBox02 Nova since 2.8.4). Trezor One is not supported. Hardware-wallet wallets are watch-only until the device signs over USB; they cannot take part in CoinJoin.
interfaces.authentication: PIN and optional passphrase entered on the device.

interfaces.description: PSBT workflow (enable 'PSBT workflow' in Wallet Settings): 'Save PSBT file' for microSD signing on Coldcard; the signed -final.txn is broadcast with the Broadcaster tool. Coldcard 'Export Wallet > Wasabi Wallet' skeleton file (new-wallet.json) imports a watch-only wallet. No QR-based PSBT exchange is documented.
Bitcoin P2P network: since 2.8.0 wallets download BIP158 compact block filters and blocks from P2P peers instead of a central Wasabi server, over Tor by default.

Bundled Tor (0.4.9.13 in 2.8.4) started and controlled by Wasabi; UseTor Enabled (default), Disabled or EnabledOnlyRunning (connect-only mode for an already-running Tor, used on Tails and Whonix). SOCKS and control ports can be set with --torsocksport and --torcontrolport, the Tor binary with --torfolder, bridges with TorBridges.

cli: wassabee.exe (GUI) and wassabeed.exe (daemon) accept --network=main|testnet|signet|regtest ('testnet' means testnet4 since 2.7.0), --datadir=<path>, --usetor=Enabled|Disabled|EnabledOnlyRunning (true/false also accepted; forced off on regtest), --torfolder, --torsocksport, --torcontrolport, --torbridges, --terminatetoronexit, --bitcoinrpcendpoint=<http://host:port> (stored in Config.json as BitcoinRpcEndPoint), --bitcoinrpccredentialstring=<rpcuser:rpcpassword or cookiefile=<path>>, --coordinatoruri, --coordinatoridentifier, --jsonrpcserverenabled, --jsonrpcuser, --jsonrpcpassword, --jsonrpcserverprefixes, --rpconionenabled, --downloadnewversion, --blockonly, --loglevel, --logmodes, --wallet=<name> (repeatable, opens wallets at start-up), --dustthreshold, --maxcoinjoinminingfeerate, --absolutemininputcount, --exchangerateprovider, --feerateestimationprovider, --externaltransactionbroadcaster, --dropunconfirmedtransactionsafterdays, --experimentalfeatures, --enablegpu, --version, --help. Environment variables WASABI_<SWITCH> (for example WASABI_NETWORK=testnet). Contrib/CLI/wcli in the repository wraps the JSON-RPC server.
remoteManagement: Only through the optional JSON-RPC server (loopback by default; optionally an onion service with --rpconionenabled). wassabeed.exe runs headless. There is no SSH or admin API. BTCortex should use only getstatus (read-only) and stop (graceful shutdown) and never call spending, CoinJoin or key-listing methods without an explicit user action.
nodeCompatibility: Optional own-node connection over Bitcoin Core JSON-RPC (Config.json keys BitcoinRpcEndPoint and BitcoinRpcCredentialString; empty by default on mainnet; testnet4 default http://localhost:48332, signet http://localhost:38332, regtest http://localhost:18443). The node is used for BIP158 filters (2.8.0 fetches them over RPC in batches, only while the node is running and synchronised; requires blockfilterindex=1 on the node), blocks, fee estimates and broadcasting; anything unavailable falls back to the default mechanisms (P2P peers, mempool.space). Credentials are 'rpcuser:rpcpassword' or a cookie file (the 2.8.4 migration code writes 'cookiefile=<path>'). Wasabi creates no wallet inside Bitcoin Core, so the removal of legacy wallets and importmulti in Core 30 does not affect it (inferred from the documented node uses). The FAQ states that pruned nodes are supported provided BIP158 filters are enabled; blocks below the prune height then come from P2P peers. 2.8.4's RPC client uses getblock with verbosity 3, which exists since Bitcoin Core 23.0 (inference). The documentation names Bitcoin Core, Bitcoin Knots and libbitcoin as full-node examples, but a Knots node at 29.4.1 or later follows a hard-forked chain and must not be wired to Wasabi.

dependencies.notes: Own node over RPC: server=1, blockfilterindex=1 (compatible with pruning), RPC on loopback with cookie or rpcauth credentials. Without it Wasabi uses P2P compact filters from random peers.
Wasabi bundles and runs its own Tor by default. With UseTor=EnabledOnlyRunning it connects to an already-running Tor instead; avoid two Tor instances competing for the same SOCKS/control ports.
HWI ships inside Wasabi (2.0.8 updated it to 3.0.0, 2.3.0 to 3.1.0); BTCortex does not need to install it for Wasabi.
Hardware wallets via HWI over USB, or Coldcard via PSBT files on microSD. CoinJoin is not possible with hardware-wallet keys.

networking: Outbound only by default and routed through Tor: Bitcoin P2P peers (filters and blocks), mempool.space (ExchangeRateProvider, FeeRateEstimationProvider and ExternalTransactionBroadcaster all default to MempoolSpace), the user-selected CoinJoin coordinator (CoordinatorUri is empty by default since zkSNACKs closed) and update checks (DownloadNewVersion true by default). Optional Bitcoin Core RPC (for example http://127.0.0.1:8332). Optional JSON-RPC listener on 127.0.0.1:37128 (off by default on mainnet). Bundled Tor uses local SOCKS and control ports chosen by Wasabi unless overridden. No inbound ports otherwise.
storage: Installer about 99 MB and ZIP about 96 MB (2.8.4). The size of the data directory (headers, filter cache, wallets, logs) was not measured. 2.8.0 added wallet-birthday checkpoints and a filter checkpoint at height 950 000, so new wallets skip earlier history.
resources: Not documented. GPU rendering is on by default (EnableGpu). The daemon wassabeed.exe is described as minimising CPU, GPU, memory and bandwidth use.
security: Privacy relies on Tor plus client-side filtering; the documentation strongly advises against disabling Tor. CoinJoin needs a third-party coordinator that the user chooses: since 2.2.0 the client only joins rounds without a coordination fee and pays only mining fees, the coordinator sets the round's mining fee rate (capped by MaxCoinJoinMiningFeeRate, default 50) and may receive decomposition leftovers of up to 10 000 sats; WabiSabi prevents the coordinator from linking inputs to outputs, but it sees registered inputs and can ban them. BTCortex must never pick a coordinator. JSON-RPC has no TLS, some methods work without the wallet password because the wallet file is readable, and send/startcoinjoin carry passwords in request bodies: keep it disabled unless needed and never log its traffic. Release verification: per-file .asc and SHA256SUMS.asc signed with the zkSNACKs OpenPGP key 6FB3 872B 5D42 292F 5992 0797 8563 4832 8949 861E (RSA-2048, 'zkSNACKs <zksnacks@gmail.com>', valid until 2028-02-24; PGP.txt in the repository), still used for 2.8.x per the installation guide; the MSI is Authenticode-signed (Lucas Ontivero). 2.8.4 deprecates the 'compatibility passphrase' feature (users seeing its warning should create a new wallet) and ignores headers from longer chains with less accumulated work. Legal context (neutral): zkSNACKs blocked US persons from its websites and products in April 2024 and stopped coordinating on 2024-06-01 citing the need for more legal certainty; whether operating or using a CoinJoin coordinator is regulated depends on the jurisdiction (compare the 2025 US convictions of the Samourai Wallet founders for conspiracy to operate an unlicensed money transmitting business).
licenceNotes: MIT (LICENSE.md; NOTICE.md lists third-party components). The packages bundle Tor and HWI binaries under their own licences. Redistribution is allowed; downloading the official artefacts at install time avoids bundling them in BTCortex.
integrationMechanisms: Download Wasabi-<version>-win-x64.zip (or the MSI) and its .asc from the GitHub release; verify the OpenPGP signature against the pinned fingerprint 6FB3872B5D42292F59920797856348328949861E (optionally also SHA256SUMS.asc), then the SHA-256
Zero-touch install without elevation: extract the ZIP into a versioned per-user directory under %LOCALAPPDATA% and create BTCortex-owned shortcuts

Unattended MSI alternative (needs elevation): msiexec /i Wasabi-<version>.msi /qn /norestart; per-machine install to C:\Program Files\WasabiWallet\; MajorUpgrade replaces older versions and refuses downgrades

Managed launch with documented startup parameters: wassabee.exe --network=main --bitcoinrpcendpoint=http://127.0.0.1:8332 --bitcoinrpccredentialstring=cookiefile=<Core data directory>\.cookie --downloadnewversion=false (parameters are not persisted)

Persistent pre-configuration only while Wasabi is closed (the '.wasabi-lock' file in %APPDATA%\WalletWasabi\Client must not be locked): read Config.json, require ConfigVersion 4, set BitcoinRpcEndPoint and BitcoinRpcCredentialString, keep every other key, write atomically and keep a backup
Prepare the managed node: blockfilterindex=1 (works with pruning) and server=1, then wait for getindexinfo to report the basic block filter index as synced
Leave CoordinatorUri empty and explain in the UI that CoinJoin requires a coordinator chosen by the user
Health and shutdown: process and lock-file detection; JSON-RPC getstatus and stop only if the user enabled the JSON-RPC server
Detect existing installations: MSI UpgradeCode {D8E80773-D8CF-4031-B8B3-AA750AF0B413}, C:\Program Files\WasabiWallet\wassabee.exe and %APPDATA%\WalletWasabi\Client

feasibility.notes: Official, OpenPGP-verifiable x64 ZIP and MSI; documented startup parameters override Config.json without modifying it, so BTCortex can launch Wasabi wired to the managed node and with its own updater disabled. Persisted pre-configuration means editing Config.json while Wasabi is closed: the decoder is strict (an unreadable file stops start-up) and the schema changed in 2.6.0 (BackendUri, UseBitcoinRpc), 2.7.0 (per-network files) and 2.8.0 (ConfigVersion 4, no indexer URI), so the writer must be version-gated; the public FAQ still shows the older UseBitcoinRpc key. CoinJoin depends on a user-chosen third-party coordinator and carries jurisdiction-dependent legal questions, which BTCortex must surface rather than decide. P2 because Wasabi is an optional privacy wallet, not part of the essential Phase 5 integrations; it does work with the pruned test node once blockfilterindex=1 is set (FAQ statement, not tested).

notes: History: Wasabi 1.x (zkSNACKs, Tor plus ZeroLink CoinJoin) is superseded by 2.x (WabiSabi). 2.0.8 (2024-06-01) added custom coordinators, Tor bridges and Tails/Whonix connect-only mode after the zkSNACKs coordinator shut down. 2.6.0 was the first version to synchronise without a central server. 2.7.0 (2025-08-30) stopped bundling bitcoind binaries, introduced per-network config files and Bitcoin RPC endpoints (including onion RPC) and made full RBF the default. 2.8.0 (2026-06-27) introduced P2P compact-filter synchronisation, wallet-birthday checkpoints, paying inside a CoinJoin, payment batching, sub-1 sat/vB fees, signet, an experimental Scheme scripting language and .NET 10. On 2026-10-21 master removed the remaining indexer ('Remove Indexer (#15190)'), so the next release is expected to drop it entirely. Supported standards listed by the documentation: BIP21, 32, 38, 39, 44, 72, 78 (Payjoin), 84, 86, 125, 141, 143, 144, 157, 158, 173, 174, 341 and 352 (sending to Silent Payments; receiving 'coming soon'), plus SLIP-39; BIP37 and BIP69 are explicitly not supported. No multisig, no miniscript, no BIP329 label export documented, no QR PSBT exchange.

name: Caravan
purpose: Stateless, browser-based multisig coordinator (the React single-page 'Caravan Coordinator'), originally Unchained's and now developed in the caravan-bitcoin monorepo. It derives multisig addresses from xpubs, builds and broadcasts transactions and collects signatures from hardware wallets, files or BC-UR 2 QR signers, using public block-explorer APIs or a private Bitcoin Core node.

maintenance.evidence: caravan-coordinator@1.19.2 released 2026-07-20 (1.19.0 on 2026-03-02 added BC-UR 2); @caravan/wallets@0.11.0 2026-08-22; @caravan/psbt@2.1.1 and @caravan/bitcoin@0.4.6 2026-09-17. Latest commits 2026-10-15 (signature audit refactor, PR #517 from an Unchained contributor). Docker Hub caravanbitcoin/coordinator:1.19.2 pushed 2026-07-20.

platforms.windowsVersions: Not stated upstream; any Windows version that runs a current Chromium-based browser (direct device access relies on browser USB APIs)
platforms.windowsDistribution: No Windows package. Options: the hosted site (caravanmultisig.com; also linked: caravan-bitcoin.github.io/caravan and caravan-coordinator.vercel.app), the official Docker image caravanbitcoin/coordinator (linux/amd64 and linux/arm64; container port 80), or a static build from source with Node.js >= 24 and npm >= 11.10 (npm run build:coordinator).
platforms.other: Any operating system with a modern browser; npm libraries @caravan/bitcoin, @caravan/psbt, @caravan/wallets, @caravan/clients, @caravan/multisig for developers.

interfaces.description: Static single-page application with hash routing (for example http://localhost:8000/#), served by the hosted sites, the Docker image (nginx, container port 80) or vite (preview 4173, development 5173).

Private client: Bitcoin Core JSON-RPC called from the browser (axios POST, HTTP basic auth, no timeout) through a CORS-adding reverse proxy (upstream nginx template: listen 8080, proxy to 127.0.0.1:8332). Uses an optional walletName for a watch-only descriptor wallet that the user creates (createwallet blank=true disable_private_keys=true load_on_startup=true). Calls importdescriptors (timestamp "now", or 0 when a rescan is requested), getwalletinfo, listunspent, gettransaction, getreceivedbyaddress, listtransactions, getmempoolentry, estimatesmartfee, getrawtransaction and sendrawtransaction.
interfaces.authentication: RPC user and password sent as HTTP basic authentication from the browser

interfaces.description: Public client: Esplora-style APIs at https://unchained.mempool.space (default) or https://blockstream.info: /address/{a}/utxo, /address/{a}, /address/{a}/txs, /tx/{txid}, /tx/{txid}/hex, POST /tx, /v1/fees/recommended, /v1/mining/blocks/fee-rates/all, /fee-estimates; mainnet and testnet only.

Direct keystores from the browser: Trezor (@trezor/transport; the README still says Trezor Bridge is required), Ledger and Ledger v2 (wallet policy registration with policy HMACs), BitBox and Jade (metadata, xpub export, multisig signing, address confirmation, policy registration where supported).
interfaces.authentication: On-device confirmation

interfaces.description: BC-UR 2 (BCUR2 keystore, 1.19.0+) for xpub import, PSBT signing, wallet registration and address confirmation with QR signers.

Wallet configuration JSON (MultisigWalletConfig: name, uuid, quorum.requiredSigners and totalSigners, addressType, extendedPublicKeys[] with xfp, bip32Path and xpub, network, ledgerPolicyHmacs[]); indirect signing for Coldcard, Hermit and custom keys through files or text; PSBT import and export.

remoteManagement: Nothing to manage: the coordinator is stateless. A node on another machine can serve as the private client only through an authenticated, CORS-restricted HTTPS proxy; an SSH tunnel or a private network is preferable to exposing RPC.
nodeCompatibility: Private client: Bitcoin Core with RPC and wallets enabled, a user-created watch-only descriptor wallet and a reverse proxy that adds CORS headers (Bitcoin Core sends none). Only descriptor-wallet RPCs are used by the client (a legacy importmulti helper remains in bitcoind.ts but the client calls importdescriptors), so the code path is compatible with Core 30.x and 31.1. txindex is not required for wallet transactions. The README says users must re-index when an imported wallet's history predates the import and txindex is off; a descriptor rescan (timestamp 0) normally suffices on an unpruned node, while a pruned node cannot serve history below its prune height. Regtest only through the private client with an uploaded configuration. Public client: Unchained's mempool.space instance or Blockstream's Esplora. Bitcoin Knots >= 29.4.1 follows a different chain.

dependencies.notes: A private Bitcoin Core node behind a CORS proxy, or a public Esplora/mempool API (unchained.mempool.space by default).
Keystores in @caravan/wallets; QR signers through BC-UR 2.

networking: Served from whatever origin hosts it (hosted HTTPS sites, Docker nginx on container port 80, vite 4173/5173). The browser calls unchained.mempool.space or blockstream.info in public mode, or the user's CORS proxy in private mode (upstream example: http://localhost:8080 for a node on 127.0.0.1:8332). Device libraries may contact vendor services (not checked).
storage: Stateless: Caravan 'does not itself store any data'; the user must keep the wallet configuration file and the addresses, redeem scripts and BIP32 paths it creates. In private mode the watch-only descriptor wallet lives in Bitcoin Core.
resources: Negligible at run time (static web application). Building from source needs Node.js >= 24 and npm >= 11.10.
security: Caravan holds no keys; signatures are produced on devices or by external signers after explicit user action. Loading the coordinator from a hosted origin means trusting remote JavaScript that sees xpubs and, in private mode, the node's RPC credentials; a locally served copy is preferable. The CORS proxy must allow only the Caravan origin and RPC must stay on loopback; the README stresses that CORS headers 'are essential to protecting the security of your coins'. Public mode reveals every wallet address to the API operator (Unchained's mempool.space instance or Blockstream). Supply-chain hardening: a 7-day npm min-release-age in .npmrc.
licenceNotes: MIT ('Copyright (c) 2024 Caravan'); BTCortex may serve a built copy with the notice.
integrationMechanisms: Open the hosted coordinator or a locally served build in the user's Chromium-based browser (external launcher); do not embed it in BTCortex's WebView2 until WebHID/WebUSB device access has been tested there
Optionally run the official caravanbitcoin/coordinator image on loopback (managed Docker) or serve the static build from BTCortex's sidecar
Generate a Caravan wallet configuration JSON from xpubs or a sortedmulti descriptor that BTCortex already holds (watch-only)

For private mode: create the watch-only descriptor wallet with load_on_startup=true and a dedicated rpcauth user with an rpcwhitelist limited to the RPCs Caravan uses, and expose them through a loopback CORS proxy restricted to the Caravan origin

feasibility.notes: Caravan is maintained and MIT-licensed but has no Windows artefact: it is a static web application reached through a hosted site, a Docker image or a source build. Private-node mode needs a CORS proxy and RPC credentials in the browser, which BTCortex would have to provide carefully. Launching it (with a generated wallet configuration file) is easy; full private-node wiring is a later step. Priority P3.

notes: Multisig only. Hermit (Unchained's shard-based signer) is supported as an indirect keystore. PSBTv2 handling was fixed in @caravan/psbt 2.1.1. No miniscript, Taproot multisig or BIP329 label support was found. The repository moved from unchained-capital/caravan to caravan-bitcoin/caravan and the libraries were renamed from unchained-bitcoin and unchained-wallets to @caravan/bitcoin and @caravan/wallets.

The multisig address types offered (historically P2SH, P2SH-P2WSH and P2WSH) and the absence of Taproot multisig were not confirmed from the current enum.
Which QR devices work through BC-UR 2 was not verified.
The README's statement that Trezor Bridge is required may be outdated (see the trezor entry).
WebHID/WebUSB/WebSerial availability inside WebView2 for embedding Caravan was not tested.
The coordinator's downloadable wallet file may carry additional fields (for example client and starting address index); only the MultisigWalletConfig interface was read.
Whether device libraries contact vendor services at run time was not checked.

name: Blockstream App
purpose: Blockstream's Bitcoin, Liquid and Lightning wallet (formerly Blockstream Green). The Qt desktop app offers singlesig wallets on Electrum servers (Blockstream's by default or a personal server), Blockstream-cosigned 2-of-2 and 2-of-3 multisig accounts, watch-only wallets, Jade and Ledger hardware-wallet support and Tor.

maintenance.evidence: Release 3.6.0 published 2026-09-21 (3.5.4 2026-08-31, 3.5.0 2026-08-11, 3.0.0 2026-01-13). Latest master commit 2026-09-21. Renamed from Blockstream Green to Blockstream App in 2.0.26 (2025-07-10); 3.5.0 removed the remaining 'Green' references. The desktop app is still offered on blockstream.com/app (3.6.0 for Windows, macOS and Linux).

platforms.windowsDistribution: BlockstreamSetup-x86_64.exe (189 MB; Inno Setup with PrivilegesRequired=admin, 64-bit mode, installs under the common Program Files folder, silently installs vc_redist.x64 when MSVCP140.dll is older than 14.40, removes old 'Blockstream Green' shortcuts and registry keys). No portable build. SHA256SUMS.asc (clearsigned) in the GitHub release; the website serves desktop installers from Blockstream's update server.
platforms.other: macOS arm64, x86_64 and universal .dmg; Linux x86_64 AppImage; Android and iOS apps from separate repositories (green_android, green_ios).

interfaces.description: Qt/QML desktop GUI built on Blockstream's GDK wallet library; single-instance (KDSingleApplication) with a watchdog process that relaunches the UI.
interfaces.authentication: PIN for software wallets; device PIN for Jade and Ledger.

interfaces.description: Singlesig wallets use Electrum servers: Blockstream's by default, or a personal server (settings use_personal_node, bitcoin_electrum_url, testnet_electrum_url, liquid_electrum_url, liquid_testnet_electrum_url, enable_electrum_tls; personal server support since 1.0.5; configurable gap limit gap_limit since 3.6.0). SPV checking (enable_spv) for singlesig.
Blockstream's Green multisig backend (through GDK) for 2-of-2 accounts with a Blockstream-held co-signing key and timelocked recovery, and 2-of-3 accounts (Bitcoin only, creation restored in 3.6.0).
interfaces.authentication: Wallet login plus optional two-factor methods (Telegram 2FA removed in 3.5.0).

interfaces.description: Blockstream Jade (and Jade Plus) over USB, including firmware updates and genuine checks; Ledger devices for singlesig Bitcoin (since 1.1.0) and Liquid on Nano S (2.0.4).
interfaces.authentication: Device PIN.

interfaces.description: Jade QR Connect and air-gapped Jade signing for watch-only wallets (3.5.0); QR scanning for send and receive.
Built-in Tor toggle (use_tor) or a SOCKS proxy (use_proxy, proxy_host, proxy_port); also --tor and --proxy on the command line.

settings.ini (QSettings INI) in the data directory's 'app' subfolder, written with a 2-second debounce; the data directory defaults to QStandardPaths AppLocalDataLocation with organisation 'Blockstream' and application name 'Green', or --datadir.

cli: Blockstream executable: --datadir <path>, --tempdatadir, --tor enabled|disabled, --proxy <host:port>, --analytics enabled|disabled, --testnet, --jade enabled|disabled (default enabled), --debugjade, --updatecheckperiod <seconds> (default 3600), --channel <name> (default latest), --debug, --ui (used internally: the watchdog relaunches the UI with --ui --datadir), --help, --version, and a positional bitcoin:, liquidnetwork: or lightning: URI that is forwarded to an already-running instance.
remoteManagement: None.
nodeCompatibility: No Bitcoin Core RPC support. Singlesig wallets can use a personal Electrum server, so a BTCortex-managed Fulcrum or electrs works - which in turn requires an unpruned node. Multisig accounts always depend on Blockstream's backend regardless of the personal-server setting. With only the pruned test node, the app cannot be pointed at local infrastructure.

dependencies.notes: Personal Electrum server for singlesig wallets (use_personal_node=true, bitcoin_electrum_url, enable_electrum_tls).
First-party hardware wallet integration over USB and QR, including firmware updates.
Ledger support for singlesig Bitcoin and Liquid (Nano S) per the changelog.
Built-in Tor toggle; an external Tor SOCKS proxy can be used through the proxy setting.

networking: Outbound: Blockstream Electrum servers or a personal Electrum server (singlesig), Blockstream's Green backend (multisig), the update server (checks every 3600 s by default), Lightning and swap services for the Lightning beta and Liquid features (Boltz tasks in the source), price and buy-bitcoin partner services, and the analytics endpoint when analytics are enabled. Optional built-in Tor or SOCKS proxy. No inbound ports.
security: Software singlesig wallets are hot wallets unless Jade or Ledger is used; the beta Lightning node (3.5.0) for mainnet software wallets adds hot-wallet risk. Multisig accounts rely on Blockstream as co-signer, with timelocked recovery. Release verification: SHA256SUMS.asc clearsigned with Blockstream's key 04BE BF2E 35A2 AF2F FDF1 FA5D E7F0 54AA 2E76 E792 (keyserver.ubuntu.com); the help article gives hash-check commands only for Linux and macOS. The installer requires elevation and silently installs the Visual C++ runtime. Analytics can be disabled (--analytics disabled). BTCortex must never import mnemonics into the app.
licenceNotes: GNU GPL version 3 per the repository licence; whether 'only' or 'or later' applies was not determined. Blockstream trademarks apply to the name and logo.
integrationMechanisms: Download BlockstreamSetup-x86_64.exe and SHA256SUMS.asc from the GitHub release; verify the clearsigned checksums against the pinned fingerprint 04BEBF2E35A2AF2FFDF1FA5DE7F054AA2E76E792, then the SHA-256
Unattended install with standard Inno Setup switches (/VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART) from an elevated context (untested)
Launch with --tor enabled or --proxy 127.0.0.1:<socks port> and, for an isolated profile, --datadir <path>

When BTCortex manages an Electrum server: write use_personal_node=true, bitcoin_electrum_url=<host:port> and enable_electrum_tls in settings.ini while the app is closed (path inferred, see unverified claims)
Open bitcoin: payment URIs in the running instance by launching the executable with the URI

feasibility.notes: Verifiable x64 installer (admin only) and clear command-line switches for Tor and proxy. Pre-configuring a personal Electrum server is feasible (settings.ini keys from source) but only useful with an unpruned node and an Electrum server, and multisig always uses Blockstream's backend. P3: overlaps with Sparrow and Electrum for self-hosted use; mainly relevant to Jade owners.

notes: Feature set beyond Bitcoin: Liquid (singlesig and multisig, AMP2 accounts on testnet in 3.5.0), Lightning via Liquid swaps and a beta Lightning node (3.5.0), paying BOLT12 offers, LNURL, BIP353 and Lightning addresses (3.4.0 to 3.6.0). Watch-only: singlesig import with xpubs and output descriptors (2.0.5). PSBT file import or export is not mentioned in the changelog. 3.0.0 (2026-01-13) redesigned the app.

sources.title: Blockstream help: verify the Blockstream app binaries

unverifiedClaims: The settings path %LOCALAPPDATA%\Blockstream\Green\app\settings.ini is inferred from Qt's AppLocalDataLocation (organisation 'Blockstream', application 'Green') and GetDataFile('app', 'settings.ini'); it was not observed on Windows.
Default values of the settings (for example whether use_tor is off by default) were not visible in the fetched source.
Silent installation with Inno Setup switches was not tested; supported Windows versions are not documented.
That the personal Electrum server setting applies only to singlesig wallets is inferred from the architecture (multisig uses Blockstream's backend), not from current official documentation.
Whether the Windows installer is Authenticode-signed was not checked.

name: Bitcoin Keeper
purpose: Open-source mobile (Android, iOS) Bitcoin wallet focused on multi-key (multisig and miniscript) vaults, inheritance and emergency keys, with a cross-platform Keeper Desktop companion app that connects USB hardware signers to the mobile app.

maintenance.evidence: Bitcoin Keeper v2.6.3 published 2026-10-07 (v2.6.2 2026-10-06, v2.5.17 2026-10-02, v2.5.13 2026-06-03). Keeper Desktop v0.2.5 published 2026-10-06 (v0.2.4 2025-06-11, v0.2.0 2025-02-06). Originally developed by BitHyve UK Limited; the website now describes Keeper as a community-run project maintained by independent developers, and the bithyve repositories redirect to the KeeperCommunity GitHub organisation.

platforms.windowsDistribution: Only the Keeper Desktop companion runs on Windows; the wallet itself is a mobile app. Keeper Desktop 0.2.5 ships Keeper.Desktop_0.2.5_x64-setup.exe and Keeper.Desktop_0.2.5_x64_en-US.msi (Tauri bundles) with SHA256SUMS.txt and SHA256SUMS.txt.asc. Keeper Desktop 0.2.5 must be paired with Bitcoin Keeper mobile 2.6.3.
platforms.other: Android (Google Play; signed APK on GitHub) and iOS (App Store). Keeper Desktop also for macOS (x64 and aarch64 .dmg) and Linux (AppImage, .deb, .rpm).

interfaces.description: Mobile app for creating and operating multi-key wallets (presets 2-of-3 and 3-of-5 or custom), a fixed 2-of-3 collaborative wallet, timelocked wallets, inheritance and emergency keys, and an optional server key held by Keeper's servers that cannot spend alone.
interfaces.authentication: App PIN on the phone; signers authenticate on their own devices.

interfaces.description: Keeper Desktop (Tauri app) lets the mobile app use USB hardware signers: add a device, run a health check, verify addresses and sign. Release coverage names miniscript support with BitBox02, COLDCARD, Jade and Ledger (desktop 0.2.0) and the BitBox02 pairing code.
interfaces.authentication: PIN and passphrase on the hardware device.

interfaces.description: The mobile app synchronises through Electrum servers and offers an Electrum server management interface for the user's own server, with Tor support (third-party index); a server can be chosen during initial setup.

nodeCompatibility: No direct Bitcoin Core connection. The mobile app talks to Electrum servers; a BTCortex-managed Fulcrum or electrs (unpruned node) can be offered to the phone over Tor or a private network. Keeper Desktop does not need a node.

dependencies.notes: Own Electrum server for the mobile app, reachable from the phone (onion service or private network).
Signers used through Keeper Desktop (USB) or directly from the phone; miniscript vaults with BitBox02, COLDCARD, Tapsigner, Jade and Ledger per the 2.0.1 release coverage.

networking: Mobile app: Electrum server connections (default servers or the user's own), Keeper's servers for the optional server key and assisted server backup. The Keeper Desktop pairing mechanism with the mobile app is not documented in the README.
security: Optional server key and assisted backups place encrypted material on Keeper's infrastructure; the server key cannot spend alone. Mobile releases are signed with the 'Hexa Team' OpenPGP key 389F 4CAD A078 5AC0 E28A 0C18 1BEB DE26 1DC3 CF62 (SHA256SUM.asc and a detached KEEPER_DETACHED_SIGN.sign). Keeper Desktop release notes ask users to verify SHA256SUMS.txt.asc against 'the Keeper release signing key' without printing its fingerprint. BTCortex must never import mnemonics into Keeper; its role is limited to providing an Electrum endpoint and, optionally, installing Keeper Desktop.
licenceNotes: MIT for both the mobile app and Keeper Desktop (repository licences). The website states that all features are available without a subscription.
integrationMechanisms: Expose a BTCortex-managed Electrum server endpoint (onion address or private-network address plus TLS fingerprint) for the user to enter in the mobile app
Optionally download Keeper Desktop (x64 MSI or NSIS setup.exe) with SHA256SUMS.txt and .asc, verify, install and launch it for USB signer sessions (signing key fingerprint still to be confirmed)

feasibility.notes: The wallet runs on phones, so BTCortex can only provide an Electrum endpoint and, at most, install and launch Keeper Desktop. The Keeper Desktop signing key fingerprint is not published in the release notes and the pairing mechanism is undocumented, so even the launcher level needs more research. P3.

notes: Keeper Desktop is a Tauri (Rust plus Vite) application; earlier desktop releases added Trezor Safe 5, Ledger Stax and Flex and USB options for Coldcard and Jade (0.1.3, per release coverage). The README's clone URL still points to bithyve/keeper-desktop although the repository now lives under KeeperCommunity.

name: Trezor Suite
purpose: SatoshiLabs' official companion app for Trezor devices: firmware installation and updates, device setup and authenticity checks, single-signature Bitcoin accounts, and a configurable Blockbook or (desktop only) Electrum back end with built-in Tor.

maintenance.evidence: Desktop v26.9.3 published 2026-10-01 (installer signature created 2026-09-23), v26.9.2 on 2026-09-16, v26.10.1 pre-release on 2026-10-15; latest commit on develop 2026-10-16; repository not archived.

platforms.windowsVersions: 64-bit Windows; minimum version not stated in a retrievable source (Electron 43.2.0, which targets Windows 10 and later)
platforms.windowsDistribution: Trezor-Suite-26.9.3-win-x64.exe (158 791 912 bytes): electron-builder NSIS assisted installer (oneClick: false, no perMachine setting, so the install-mode page offers per-user or all-users; default per-user path %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Trezor Suite\Trezor Suite.exe). Authenticode-signed with signtool (publisher names 'SatoshiLabs, s.r.o.' and 'Trezor Company s.r.o.'); detached OpenPGP signature Trezor-Suite-<version>-win-x64.exe.asc; latest.yml and .blockmap feed electron-updater from data.trezor.io. Bundles tor, coinjoin and Bluetooth helper binaries. No portable build, no arm64 Windows build.
platforms.other: macOS (x64 and arm64 DMG/ZIP), Linux AppImage (x86_64, arm64), Android and iOS apps, and Suite Web (WebUSB in Chromium-based browsers).

interfaces.description: Electron desktop application (app ID com.trezor.suite, user data directory %APPDATA%\@trezor\suite-desktop).
interfaces.authentication: Device PIN/passphrase on the Trezor; optional app-level biometric unlock (bioAuthSettings).

interfaces.description: Runtime flags: --tor (start with Tor enabled), --disable-updater / --enable-updater, --pre-release, --updater-url=URL, --bridge-daemon (daemon mode without UI), --bridge-daemon-show-ui, --log-level=NAME, --log-write, --log-path, --log-file, --offline-mode (experimental, does not control tor/coinjoin subprocesses), --bridge-test, --open-devtools, --remove-user-data-on-start (E2E testing; destructive).
Internal 'node bridge' (@trezor/transport-bridge, a JavaScript clone of trezord-go) on 127.0.0.1:21328, started when no external bridge is running; used by Suite and Trezor Connect clients.
interfaces.authentication: Origin allow-list (trezor.io, sldev.cz, localhost, the Trezor onion address); no credentials.

interfaces.description: Client for a custom Electrum server, desktop only, entered as host:port:t (TCP) or host:port:s (TLS), for example 127.0.0.1:50002:s or an .onion host. Custom Blockbook URLs are the other back-end type.
Bundled Tor (torSettings defaults: SOCKS 127.0.0.1:9050, control port 9051) or an external Tor (useExternalTor, externalPort).

Experimental MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for AI agents at http://127.0.0.1:21340/mcp, off by default (Settings, Experimental Features). Tools include trezor_get_address, trezor_get_public_key, trezor_get_account_info, trezor_send_transaction (broadcast defaults to true), trezor_push_transaction and trezor_sign_message.
interfaces.authentication: Token passed as a URL query parameter.

interfaces.description: electron-store file config.json in the user data directory with winBounds, updateSettings, themeSettings, torSettings, bridgeSettings (doNotStartOnStartup, usbImplementation), traySettings, connectSettings, bioAuthSettings, mcpSettings and isDebugModeActive. Wallet settings, remembered wallets and custom back ends live in the renderer's storage, not in this file.

cli: "%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Trezor Suite\Trezor Suite.exe" [--tor] [--disable-updater] [--log-level=debug --log-write]. Unattended install (electron-builder assisted-installer switches, not tested with this installer): Trezor-Suite-<version>-win-x64.exe /S /currentuser (per-user, no elevation) or /S /allusers (elevated), optional /D=<directory>.
remoteManagement: None. Suite is an interactive desktop application; its bridge and MCP server listen on loopback only.
nodeCompatibility: Does not talk to Bitcoin Core. Default back end: Trezor-operated Blockbook servers. Alternatives: a custom Blockbook (blockbook) or, on desktop only, a custom Electrum server (fulcrum, electrs, electrumx) under Settings, coin settings, custom back end. A pruned Bitcoin Core node cannot serve Suite directly, because every supported back end needs an unpruned indexer.

dependencies.notes: Companion app for Trezor devices.
Own Electrum server as custom back end (desktop only); remove the default servers for privacy.
Own Blockbook as custom back end.
Suite bundles its own tor; an external Tor SOCKS port can be used instead.
While Suite runs, its internal bridge holds the Trezor; close Suite (or stop its bridge) before signing with HWI, Sparrow or Electrum (expected behaviour, not tested).

networking: Outbound HTTPS/WebSocket to Trezor's Blockbook servers, data.trezor.io (firmware and app updates) and other Trezor services, or to the configured custom back end; optional Tor. Listens on 127.0.0.1:21328 (internal bridge) and, only if enabled, 127.0.0.1:21340 (MCP).
storage: Installer about 159 MB (26.9.3); user data in %APPDATA%\@trezor\suite-desktop (size not measured).
resources: Electron application; requirements not published in a retrievable source.
security: Downloads: verify the OpenPGP signature with the SatoshiLabs 2021 Signing Key (RSA-4096, created 2021-01-04, fingerprint EB48 3B26 B078 A4AA 1B6F 425E E21B 6950 A2EC B65C, published at trezor.io/security/satoshilabs-2021-signing-key.asc; the 26.9.3 Windows .asc was issued by this key on 2026-09-23); the 2020 key 5406 7D8B BF00 5541 81B5 AB8F 26A3 A566 62F0 E7E2 expired on 2021-01-01. Windows binaries are also Authenticode-signed. Suite auto-updates itself from data.trezor.io unless --disable-updater is used. Privacy: the default back end is Trezor's Blockbook; Suite's own-node article recommends a custom Blockbook or Electrum server. CoinJoin: Trezor shut the feature down in June 2024 after zkSNACKs stopped coordinating; PR #33361 (merged 2026-10-16) removed the dead default coordinators and affiliate server. The experimental MCP server lets local AI agents request addresses, signatures and transactions (still confirmed on the device); BTCortex must never enable it. BTCortex must not automate Suite's UI or touch its wallet storage.
licenceNotes: Trezor Reference Source License (T-RSL): source-available, granting reproduction for 'reference use'; not an open-source licence. BTCortex must not bundle or redistribute Suite; download the official installer from GitHub or trezor.io at install time.
integrationMechanisms: Download Trezor-Suite-<version>-win-x64.exe and its .asc from the GitHub release; verify the OpenPGP signature against the pinned SatoshiLabs 2021 key EB483B26B078A4AA1B6F425EE21B6950A2ECB65C and check the Authenticode signature
Install unattended per user with /S /currentuser (to be validated on a clean Windows VM)
Detect an existing installation (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Trezor Suite or the uninstall key) and the user data directory %APPDATA%\@trezor\suite-desktop
Launch with --tor when the BTCortex privacy profile is active

Show the exact custom back-end value for the user to enter (for example 127.0.0.1:50002:s for a managed Fulcrum, or an onion host); Suite stores it in renderer storage that BTCortex cannot safely pre-configure
Close Suite before HWI or Sparrow sessions; detect its bridge on 127.0.0.1:21328

feasibility.notes: Installation can be automated from a verifiable, signed artefact without elevation (per-user NSIS). The only configuration that matters to BTCortex (custom Electrum/Blockbook back end) is kept in Suite's internal renderer storage, so it cannot be pre-configured safely; config.json only holds Tor, bridge, updater and window settings and is undocumented. Launching with --tor is the only supported way to influence settings from outside.

notes: Default install path and data directory come from Trezor's own developer documentation (docs/packages/desktop-app/index.md). Suite 26.x also bundles Bluetooth support for the Safe 7 on Windows. The Electrum back end option is filtered to desktop builds (isDesktop() in BackendTypeSelect.tsx). Trezor's article 'Connect Trezor Suite to your own node' describes pointing Suite at your own Blockbook or Electrum node (only its summary was retrievable on 2026-10-21).

name: Ledger Wallet (formerly Ledger Live)
purpose: Ledger's companion app, renamed from Ledger Live to Ledger Wallet on 2025-10-23. It installs and updates Ledger OS and on-device apps such as the Bitcoin app, and manages accounts through Ledger's own explorer services.

name: BitBoxApp
purpose: Shift Crypto's companion wallet for the BitBox02: device setup, firmware upgrades, host pairing and single-signature accounts backed by Electrum servers (Shift's by default, or your own), with an optional SOCKS5/Tor proxy.

maintenance.evidence: v4.52.0 released 2026-09-15 (release candidates from 2026-08-31; Windows signature created 2026-09-11); bundles BitBox02 firmware 9.27.1.

platforms.windowsDistribution: BitBox-4.52.0-win64-installer.exe: NSIS installer with RequestExecutionLevel admin, default directory $PROGRAMFILES64\BitBox, executable BitBox.exe, uninstall entry under HKCU; per-file detached OpenPGP signature (.asc) and SHA-256 on bitbox.swiss/download (Windows 4.52.0: ab7db80c5547c559b0cc0c9487a26dd1e9916d3390130c2e14355e3cc66abb56). No portable build.
platforms.other: macOS DMG, Linux AppImage/deb/rpm, Android APK, iOS (with the Nova over Bluetooth).

interfaces.description: Qt desktop application with a Go back end.
interfaces.authentication: Optional app authentication setting; device password on the BitBox02.

interfaces.description: Configuration in %APPDATA%\bitbox: config.json (app settings: backend.proxy {useProxy, proxyAddress}; backend.btc.electrumServers [{server: 'host:port', tls: bool, pemCert: '<PEM>'}]; tbtc/rbtc/ltc equivalents; startInTestnet; fiat and unit settings), accounts.json, lightning.json, log.txt and the bitbox02, cache, lightning and notes directories. 4.52.0 restricts local permissions on these files.

Client to Electrum servers; defaults btc1-btc4.shiftcrypto.io:443 (TLS with Shift's root CA). Own servers are added under Settings, Advanced settings, 'Connect your own full node', with 'Download remote certificate' for self-signed TLS. 'If you do not remove the default servers, your own node will be added as a redundancy.'
interfaces.authentication: TLS with a pinned PEM certificate per server (pemCert).

interfaces.description: Optional Tor/SOCKS5 proxy (useProxy, proxyAddress); the in-app help suggests port 9050 for the Tor service or 9150 for Tor Browser.
Flags: --testnet, --simulator (implies testnet), --simulatorPort (default 15423), --gapLimitReceive, --gapLimitChange.

cli: "C:\Program Files\BitBox\BitBox.exe" [--testnet] [--gapLimitReceive=N] [--gapLimitChange=N]. Unattended install (standard NSIS switch, not tested): BitBox-<version>-win64-installer.exe /S from an elevated process.
remoteManagement: None.
nodeCompatibility: Electrum protocol only; no direct Bitcoin Core RPC. Works with an own fulcrum, electrs or electrumx server (unpruned node). The in-app FAQ still lists Electrum Personal Server and Bitcoin Wallet Tracker (bwt), which are incompatible with Bitcoin Core 30 and later (see the electrum-indexers-explorers notes). On a pruned-node machine the BitBoxApp cannot use the local node.

dependencies.notes: Companion app for the BitBox02.
Own Electrum server; replace (not just add to) the default Shift servers for privacy.
SOCKS5 proxy for onion servers.
Close the BitBoxApp before HWI-based tools open the BitBox02 (HWI's own error message says so).

networking: Outbound TLS to Electrum servers (default btc1-4.shiftcrypto.io:443) and Shift/partner services (exchange rates, buy/sell, marketplace, Lightning in the mobile app); optional SOCKS5 proxy. No listening ports documented.
security: Verify downloads with the 'ShiftCrypto Security <security@shiftcrypto.ch>' RSA key, fingerprint DD09 E413 0975 0EBF AE0D EF63 5092 49B0 68D2 15AE (key file bitbox.swiss/download/shiftcryptosec-509249B068D215AE.gpg.asc); the 4.52.0 Windows .asc was issued by this key on 2026-09-11. 4.52.0 requires anti-klepto-capable firmware for signing and warns about restoring external wallets. Privacy: default servers belong to Shift; adding an own node without removing the defaults keeps querying Shift. Writing config.json is only safe while BitBox.exe is not running (the app rewrites the file on settings changes).
licenceNotes: Apache-2.0; BitBox trademarks belong to Shift Crypto AG.
integrationMechanisms: Download BitBox-<version>-win64-installer.exe and .asc from the GitHub release; verify the OpenPGP signature against the pinned fingerprint DD09E41309750EBFAE0DEF63509249B068D215AE and the SHA-256 from bitbox.swiss/download
Install silently from an elevated helper (/S, to be tested); detect C:\Program Files\BitBox\BitBox.exe and %APPDATA%\bitbox

With the app closed (no BitBox.exe process), merge into %APPDATA%\bitbox\config.json: backend.btc.electrumServers = [{server: '127.0.0.1:50002', tls: true, pemCert: <managed server certificate PEM>}] and, for Tor, backend.proxy = {useProxy: true, proxyAddress: '127.0.0.1:9050'}; keep a backup and preserve unknown keys
Launch the BitBoxApp for firmware upgrades and first host pairing; remind the user to close it before HWI sessions

feasibility.notes: Connection settings live in a plain JSON file whose structure is visible in the source (config.go), so pre-configuring an own Electrum server and Tor proxy while the app is closed is feasible; the format is not documented for third parties and may change. Installation needs elevation. Useful only where an unpruned Electrum server exists (not on the 73 GB test machine).

notes: Also published: BitBoxBridge 1.6.0 (localhost:8178), which connects web wallets such as MyEtherWallet to the BitBox02; it is not needed for Bitcoin desktop wallets or HWI. BitBoxApp 4.37.3 was the last version with full BitBox01 support.
