name: COLDCARD
purpose: Bitcoin-only signing devices from Coinkite (COLDCARD Mk4, Mk5 and Q) built for air-gapped PSBT signing over microSD, NFC and (Q only) QR/BBQr, with optional USB, multisig with up to 15 co-signers, descriptor export and, on the separate EDGE firmware track, miniscript and Taproot script policies.

maintenance.evidence: Standard firmware 5.6.3 (Mk4/Mk5) and 1.5.3Q (Q) dated 2026-09-30 in releases/ChangeLog.md; releases/signatures.txt clear-signed 2026-09-30T20:27Z. Earlier: 5.6.2/1.5.2Q 2026-09-03, 5.6.1/1.5.1Q 2026-08-20, 5.5.1/1.4.1Q 2026-07-01, 5.4.5/1.3.5Q 2025-11-03. EDGE builds 6.6.1X/6.6.1QX dated 2026-08-31. Latest master commit 2026-10-09 ('Fix Shamir split share-count prompt on Mk4 and Mk5'). GitHub Releases are not used: binaries are on coldcard.com/downloads and hashes in releases/signatures.txt. Mk3/Mk2 are on their final release 4.2.0 and Mk1 on 3.0.6. ckcc-protocol 1.6.0 was published to PyPI on 2026-09-08.

platforms.windowsDistribution: Nothing has to be installed for air-gapped use: a microSD card reader, or a webcam or phone for the Q's QR and NFC. USB data uses the HID-based COLDCARD protocol (hidapi in ckcc-protocol and HWI); Virtual Disk mode emulates a 4 MB USB disk that the Q documentation lists as working on Windows. Coinkite documents download verification on Windows with Gpg4win/Kleopatra and certutil -hashfile <file> SHA256.
platforms.other: Models: Mk4 and Mk5 run the same firmware image (Mk5: 1.54-inch Gorilla Glass display, redesigned keypad, USB-C at the bottom, faster NFC, the same two secure elements from two vendors). Q: 320x240 colour LCD, 50-key QWERTY keyboard, QR scanner, two microSD slots, NFC (NFC-V), USB-C, three AAA cells or USB power; USB and NFC data can be disabled permanently by cutting PCB traces. Legacy: Mk3/Mk2 (final firmware 4.2.0), Mk1 (final 3.0.6). Companion software: any PSBT wallet; Coinkite's compatibility list names Nunchuk, Sparrow, Bitcoin Core, Electrum, BlueWallet, Casa, Cove, Fully Noded, Specter Desktop, Unchained, Wasabi Wallet, Coldcore, Theya and BTCPay Server.

interfaces.description: COLDCARD USB protocol over HID (ckcc-protocol): firmware version, chain (BTC or XTN), master fingerprint, xpubs, address display, PSBT upload and signing (approved on the device), message signing, encrypted backup, firmware upload and HSM mode. Link-layer encryption versions: v1 (legacy, default), v2, and v3 (authenticated, direction-separated keys and replay protection; opt-in, added in firmware 5.6.2/1.5.2Q and ckcc-protocol 1.6.0). HWI ships its own COLDCARD client.
interfaces.authentication: Device PIN entered on the COLDCARD; every signature is approved on the device. A BIP-39 passphrase can be sent over USB (ckcc pass), which BTCortex must never do.

interfaces.description: microSD and Virtual Disk. Signing a file <name>.psbt writes <name>-part.psbt while a multisig threshold is not yet met, otherwise <name>-signed.psbt plus <name>-final.txn (hex), or <txid>.txn when the user chooses to delete the input (firmware shared/auth.py). Exports: wallet files for Sparrow, Bitcoin Core (an importdescriptors command), Electrum and generic descriptors (single-sig with optional <0;1> multipath), XPUB export, multisig descriptors in 'pretty', bare and Bitcoin Core formats. Imports: COLDCARD multisig text files (Name:, Policy: M of N, Format: p2sh | p2wsh | p2sh-p2wsh, Derivation:, then one 'XFP: xpub' line per co-signer) or BIP-380 descriptors. Files saved to SD or Virtual Disk can be accompanied by a signature file. Cards must be FAT32 or FAT12.

COLDCARD Q only: scans PSBTs (Base64 or hex), finalised transactions, xpubs, BIP-21 URIs, addresses, multisig definitions in COLDCARD or descriptor format, SeedQR (not Compact SeedQR) and BBQr (files up to 2 MiB); shows signed PSBTs and exports as QR or BBQr. The QR documentation does not mention UR (BCR-2020-005). Mk4/Mk5 have no camera and can only display small QR codes (for example short multisig descriptors).
NFC tap (Mk4, Mk5, Q) to exchange PSBTs, signed transactions, addresses and xpubs with a phone (for example Nunchuk); also used for BSMS rounds and Key Teleport. Can be disabled in settings.

cli: ckcc (pip install "ckcc-protocol[cli]"; 1.6.0 published 2026-09-08): list, version, chain, xfp, xpub, pubkey, addr, msg, sign (-z visualises a PSBT without device interaction; finalise and broadcast options), p2sh, multisig, miniscript, upgrade (.dfu or signed .bin), backup and restore (7z-encrypted), hsm, hsm-start, user, auth, local-conf, pass, logout, reboot; -P/--plaintext disables USB link encryption. HWI: hwi enumerate, then hwi -t coldcard (or -f <fingerprint>) getxpub, getdescriptors, displayaddress, signtx, backup.
remoteManagement: None for BTCortex: the device is only reachable locally (USB, microSD, NFC, QR). COLDCARD's HSM mode (with CKBunker) signs automatically over USB under on-device spending rules; that conflicts with BTCortex's rule that signing is always explicit, so BTCortex must never enable or drive it.
nodeCompatibility: Node-agnostic signer for any coordinator that builds PSBTs. The Bitcoin Core export is an importdescriptors command with "timestamp": "now" and "range": [0, 100] for a watch-only descriptor wallet in bitcoin-core; 'now' skips historical rescans, so BTCortex should substitute the wallet birthday when it is known (and on a pruned node the birthday must not predate the prune height). Desktop coordinators: sparrow (Bitcoin Core RPC or Electrum server), electrum (coldcard plugin in upstream Electrum), specter-desktop, nunchuk, liana and bitcoin-safe; miniscript and Taproot script-path coordinators need EDGE firmware.

dependencies.notes: A coordinator or watch-only wallet builds PSBTs, tracks the wallet and broadcasts; COLDCARD only signs.
USB discovery, xpub and descriptor retrieval, address display and signing with on-device approval. Not needed for microSD, NFC or QR workflows.

networking: None. The device has no network stack; data moves over microSD, USB (HID or Virtual Disk), NFC or QR. USB and NFC can be disabled in settings, and on the Q permanently in hardware.
storage: Removable microSD formatted FAT32 or FAT12 for firmware and PSBT files; Virtual Disk is a 4 MB RAM disk exposed over USB. On-device multisig storage holds about eight M-of-3 wallets or a single M-of-15 wallet.
security: July 2026 seed-generation incident (advisory published 2026-07-30, updated 2026-08-01): a firmware bug weakened device-generated entropy and attackers regenerated affected private keys offline and stole funds. Affected: Mk2/Mk3 firmware 4.0.1 to 4.1.9 (most severe); seeds generated on Mk4/Mk5 before 5.6.0, on Q before 1.5.0Q and on EDGE before 6.6.0X/6.6.0QX (about 72 instead of 128 bits). Updating does not repair an existing seed: such wallets must be migrated to a new seed unless at least 50 private, fair dice rolls were added. TAPSIGNER, OPENDIME and SATSCARD are stated to be unaffected. BTCortex cannot tell from an xpub which firmware generated a seed, so it must show the advisory and the minimum fixed release per track (5.6.0, 1.5.0Q, 4.2.0, 6.6.0X/6.6.0QX; recommended 5.6.3/1.5.3Q) whenever a COLDCARD is detected or chosen, and never offer to 'check' a seed. Firmware authenticity: the device only runs factory-signed firmware (red CAUTION LED until an upgrade is blessed, green GENUINE LED afterwards); downloads are verified with releases/signatures.txt, a SHA-256 list clear-signed by OpenPGP key 4589779ADFC14F3327534EA8A3A31BAD5A2A5B10 (Peter D. Gray, DocHex on Keybase; issuer confirmed from the 2026-09-30 signature). Recent hardening: SIGHASH_SINGLE blocked by default, re-verification of the staged PSBT before signing, rejection of duplicate inputs and negative amounts, authenticated USB encryption v3, removal of the unused USB serial interface, warnings before externally signed firmware or downgrades. BTCortex must never send passphrases or seed material, never enable HSM mode and never sign without the user approving on the device.
licenceNotes: The firmware (COPYING-CC) and ckcc-protocol use the MIT licence text plus the 'Commons Clause' License Condition v1.0, which withholds the right to sell the software: source-available, not OSI open source. BTCortex should link to official downloads and must not redistribute firmware.
integrationMechanisms: Detect over USB with HWI (hwi enumerate: device type, path, master fingerprint); read the firmware version only on explicit request (ckcc version)
Import xpubs and descriptors from COLDCARD export files (microSD or Virtual Disk) or from Q QR/BBQr codes into a watch-only descriptor wallet in bitcoin-core or sparrow

Air-gapped PSBT round trip: write <name>.psbt to removable media, the user reviews and signs on the device, then read <name>-signed.psbt, <name>-part.psbt or <name>-final.txn, combine and finalise, and broadcast only after explicit confirmation
Generate a COLDCARD multisig text file or a BIP-380 descriptor for on-device registration, then verify a receive address with hwi displayaddress or on the device screen
Display and scan BBQr animated QR codes through a webcam for the Q
Delegate device workflows to sparrow (preferred) and show compatibility, firmware track and the 2026 advisory

feasibility.notes: HWI already supports COLDCARD over USB; microSD file naming, the multisig text format and descriptor exports are documented and stable; BBQr is a published format. Constraints: HWI is entering minimal maintenance (HWI issue #850, 2026-08-18), BBQr encoding and decoding must be implemented or delegated to Sparrow, and the 2026 RNG advisory must be surfaced.

notes: EDGE is a separate preview track (6.x 'X' builds that have 'not been qualified and tested to the same standard as a normal release'): Taproot since 6.0.0X, miniscript and MiniTapscript since 6.1.0X; BSMS (BIP-129; coordinator and signer roles, up to 15 signers, STANDARD, EXTENDED or NO_ENCRYPTION, files bsms_*.token, bsms_sr1*.dat/.txt, bsms_cr2*.dat/.txt) is documented as an EDGE-only preview. Coinkite's EDGE post names AnchorWatch, Liana and Keeper as miniscript/Taproot coordinators. Other features: COLDCARD Co-Signing (CCC), Single Signer Spending Policy (SSSP), Key Teleport between Q devices, Seed Vault, Trick PINs and Delta Mode, Codex32 and Shamir backups (5.6.3/1.5.3Q), PSBTv2 (5.6.3 adds per-input locktimes), BIP-322 signing. HWI device matrix, COLDCARD column: xpub retrieval, message signing, backup, P2PKH, P2SH-P2WPKH, P2WPKH and P2SH/P2SH-P2WSH/P2WSH multisig inputs, non-wallet and mixed inputs, display on device; no setup, wipe or recovery through software; Taproot inputs not marked as supported. HWI master (unreleased; PR #849 merged 2026-08-20) adds EDGE handling and Taproot address display.

name: Trezor (Safe 7, Safe 5, Safe 3, Model T, Model One)
purpose: Open-source hardware signing devices from SatoshiLabs. The device holds the seed, shows addresses and transaction details on its own screen and signs Bitcoin transactions only after on-device confirmation; host software (Trezor Suite, HWI, Sparrow, Electrum and others) talks to it over USB, and over Bluetooth on the Safe 7.

maintenance.evidence: core/CHANGELOG.md lists core firmware 2.12.5 dated 16 September 2026 (2.12.4 on 19 August, 2.12.3 on 24 July, 2.12.2 on 22 July, 2.12.1 on 17 June, 2.12.0 on 21 May 2026); data.trezor.io lists 2.12.5 for T3T1 (Safe 5, 19 entries) and T3W1 (Safe 7, 12 entries starting at 2.9.3, dated 21 October 2025 in the changelog). Legacy firmware for the Model One: 1.14.1 dated 18 March 2026. Repository trezor/trezor-firmware not archived, last push 2026-10-20. trezor.io/compare sells Safe 7, Safe 5 and Safe 3; the Model T and Model One are 'retired from sale, not from support' (critical security updates until at least 2036; Model T feature updates until at least 2031; Model One maintenance only).

latestStableRelease.version: core firmware 2.12.5 (Safe 3, Safe 5, Safe 7, Model T); legacy firmware 1.14.1 (Model One, 2026-03-18)

platforms.windowsDistribution: No vendor driver: both firmware lines expose Microsoft WinUSB compatible-ID descriptors (legacy/winusb.c, core/embed/io/usb/stm32/usb.c), so Windows binds WinUSB to the WebUSB interface automatically; very old Model One firmware/bootloaders use USB HID. Firmware installation, device setup, Bitcoin-only firmware and Safe 7 Bluetooth pairing are done in Trezor Suite (trezor-suite). The standalone Trezor Bridge is deprecated (trezor-bridge) and is not needed by HWI.
platforms.other: USB (USB-C on the Safe models); Bluetooth 5.0+ on the Safe 7 only (can be switched off; the device also works wired-only). Trezor Suite for Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS (iOS through Bluetooth on the Safe 7). No QR-code, microSD-PSBT or NFC signing workflows; the microSD slot on the Model T and Safe 5 is only used for SD-card PIN protection.

interfaces.description: Protocol-buffer messages over the WebUSB interface (HID on legacy Model One firmware). Initialize/GetFeatures returns a Features message without a PIN: vendor, model, internal_model (T1B1, T2T1, T2B1, T3B1, T3T1, T3W1), firmware version (major/minor/patch), bootloader_mode, firmware_present, initialized, unlocked, pin_protection, passphrase_protection, unit_btconly, capabilities, backup_availability, label and device_id. GetPublicKey (returns a BIP-380 descriptor since legacy 1.14.0), GetAddress with on-device display, SignTx, SignMessage. The Safe 7 (T3W1) requires the encrypted Trezor-Host Protocol (THP, Noise XX handshake with host pairing) for all communication.
interfaces.authentication: PIN on the device; optional passphrase (entered on the device or supplied by the host software, depending on model and settings); THP pairing (code entry) on the Safe 7.

interfaces.description: Bluetooth LE (Safe 7 only), encrypted with THP. Trezor Suite for Windows ships a Bluetooth helper (bin/bluetooth/win-x64). HWI and other Python tools have no Bluetooth transport.
interfaces.authentication: THP pairing confirmed on the device.

interfaces.description: trezorctl from the PyPI package 'trezor' (0.20.2, uploaded 2026-07-31, Python >= 3.9; 0.20.0 added THP). HWI 3.2.0 drives Trezor One, Model T, Safe 3 (T2B1 and T3B1) and Safe 5 (T3T1), but not the Safe 7.

cli: HWI: hwi enumerate; hwi -t trezor -d <path> getmasterxpub | getxpub <path> | getdescriptors --account <n> | displayaddress --desc <descriptor> | signtx <psbt>. trezorctl (get-features, btc get-public-node, btc get-address with on-device display, firmware update); BTCortex should leave firmware updates to Trezor Suite.
remoteManagement: None. The device is a local USB (or Bluetooth) peripheral of the machine running the host software; BTCortex can only use a Trezor attached to the Windows host it runs on.
nodeCompatibility: Node-agnostic: the device never talks to a node. The wallet software builds PSBTs from Bitcoin Core (directly or through Sparrow), an Electrum server or Blockbook (Suite). Bitcoin Core can use it through HWI as an external signer (-signer=<path to hwi.exe>; see bitcoin-core and hwi).

dependencies.notes: Required for firmware installation and updates, initial setup, switching to Bitcoin-only firmware, device authenticity checks and Safe 7 Bluetooth pairing.
Host software that exports xpubs/descriptors, displays addresses and sends PSBTs for on-device signing. HWI 3.2.0 does not support the Safe 7 (THP not implemented; HWI issue #775 open).
The deprecated standalone Bridge (127.0.0.1:21325) can hold the device; Trezor asks users to uninstall it.

networking: The device itself has no network access. USB, plus Bluetooth LE on the Safe 7. On the host, Trezor Suite's internal bridge listens on 127.0.0.1:21328 while Suite runs; the deprecated standalone Bridge listened on 127.0.0.1:21325.
security: Open-source firmware and bootloader; firmware images are signed by SatoshiLabs and data.trezor.io publishes per-image fingerprints (for example 2.12.5 Safe 5 universal 7fff55b9…692d, Bitcoin-only e84f251b…b5c7) for reproducible-build checks. Secure elements: the Safe 3, Safe 5 and Safe 7 use an EAL6+ certified secure element (named as Optiga on the Safe 7 page); the Safe 7 adds the TROPIC01 chip (and post-quantum SLH-DSA-128 firmware/boot verification according to Trezor). The Model One and Model T have no secure element. Advisories: Ledger Donjon's Safe 3 evaluation (reported 2024-11-12) bypassed some supply-chain countermeasures by voltage glitching (Safe 5 not affected); Ledger Donjon's TROPIC01 laser fault-injection finding (Trezor response 2026-06-03) cannot be fixed in firmware but, according to Trezor, exposes no PIN, funds or backup. Firmware security fixes relevant to Bitcoin: 2.8.7 (2025-01-22) forbids multisig-to-singlesig change and per-node paths in multisig change/receive and removed 'Unchained Capital's multisig path'; 2.10.0 (2026-01-21) BIP-39 side-channel fix; 2.11.0 (2026-03-18) multisig verification bug fix; 2.12.2 (2026-07-22) external input misidentification and new external outputs in replacement transactions; legacy 1.14.0 BIP-39 side-channel fix and 1.14.1 advanced recovery for mnemonics shorter than 24 words. For BTCortex: never ask for the PIN, passphrase or recovery words; let passphrases be entered on the device; treat device_id and label as personal data (do not log); never flash firmware itself; every signing request must be started explicitly by the user and confirmed on the device.
licenceNotes: COPYING contains the GNU GPL version 3; GitHub reports NOASSERTION because sub-components carry other licences ('-only' versus '-or-later' not checked). Trezor is a SatoshiLabs trademark. BTCortex does not redistribute firmware.
integrationMechanisms: Discover devices with hwi enumerate (HID/WebUSB; no Bridge needed) and show model, firmware version, Bitcoin-only flag and initialised/PIN/passphrase state from the Features message
Import xpubs or descriptors (hwi getdescriptors / getxpub) into a watch-only Bitcoin Core descriptor wallet or hand the device over to Sparrow
Verify receive addresses on the device screen with hwi displayaddress before marking them as verified
Send PSBTs for signing only after an explicit user action (hwi signtx; confirmation on the device); never broadcast automatically
Launch Trezor Suite for firmware updates, Bitcoin-only firmware and Safe 7 pairing

Diagnostics: detect a running Trezor Suite (internal bridge on 127.0.0.1:21328) or legacy Trezor Bridge (127.0.0.1:21325) that may hold the USB interface; flag the Safe 7 as not supported by HWI 3.2.0

feasibility.notes: High for the Model One, Model T, Safe 3 and Safe 5 through HWI (xpub export, address display, single-signature and multisig PSBT signing). The Safe 7 is blocked for HWI-based flows until HWI implements THP pairing and session persistence (issue #775, open since 2025-02-14; trezorlib 0.20.0 already supports THP). Trezor devices do not support descriptor registration or BIP-388 policies, so miniscript wallets are not possible.

notes: Model codes: T1B1 Model One, T2T1 Model T, T2B1 and T3B1 Safe 3 (two hardware revisions), T3T1 Safe 5, T3W1 Safe 7. HWI signing limits (hwilib/devices/trezor.py): multisig up to n-of-15; no arbitrary scriptPubKey/redeemScript/witnessScript; Taproot inputs cannot be combined with external inputs; Taproot needs Model One firmware >= 1.10.4 or Model T firmware >= 2.4.3; non-wallet inputs removed in firmware 1.10.6 / 2.4.4; no descriptor registration and no BIP-388 policy signing. Trezor Safe 7 specifications (trezor.io): USB-C, Bluetooth 5.0+, Qi2 wireless charging, 2.5-inch touchscreen, TROPIC01 + EAL6+ Optiga + STM32U5. A Bitcoin-only firmware build exists for every current model (url_bitcoinonly in releases.json). Trezor Suite coinjoin was discontinued in June 2024 (see trezor-suite).

The Safe 3 and Safe 5 secure element is described by trezor.io only as 'EAL6+ certified'; the Optiga part name is taken from the Safe 7 page and was not checked for the Safe 3/5.

name: Ledger (Nano S Plus, Nano X, Nano Gen5, Flex, Stax)
purpose: Secure-element hardware signers from Ledger running the closed-source Ledger OS with installable apps. Bitcoin signing is done by the open-source Ledger Bitcoin app (LedgerHQ/app-bitcoin), which supports BIP-388 wallet policies, multisig, miniscript, Taproot and MuSig2.

maintenance.evidence: Ledger Bitcoin app 2.5.1 dated 2026-09-09 (2.5.0 on 2026-07-24, 2.4.6 on 2026-03-30), built for Nano S Plus OS 1.6.1, Nano X 2.7.1, Flex 1.6.1, Stax 1.10.1 and the 'apex_p' target 1.1.1 (tags of 2026-09-09). The original Nano S stays on app 2.2.8 (nanos 2.1.0) and is no longer on the comparison page. Nano Gen5 announced 2025-10-23.

platforms.windowsVersions: Ledger requires a 64-bit computer running Windows 10 or 11 for desktop use
platforms.windowsDistribution: No vendor driver: the devices enumerate as USB HID (vendor ID 0x2C97, usage page 0xFFA0) and use Windows' built-in HID driver; HWI opens them with hidapi. The Bitcoin app and Ledger OS updates are installed only through Ledger Wallet (ledger-live).
platforms.other: USB-C on all current models (Nano X and Nano S Plus ship a USB-A to USB-C cable); Bluetooth on Nano X, Nano Gen5, Flex and Stax; NFC on Nano Gen5, Flex and Stax (comparison page). Android supports all models; the Nano S Plus 'does not work with iOS devices'. No QR or microSD signing.

interfaces.description: APDU exchange over USB HID with the Bitcoin app open. Apps >= 2.1.0 use the new protocol with wallet policies (register_wallet returns an HMAC that the host must store and send with later signing and address-display requests); apps 1.x/2.0.x use the legacy protocol. The Bitcoin app reports its name and version; the master fingerprint and xpubs at standard paths are exported without confirmation (standard BIP-87 xpubs since 2.5.0).
interfaces.authentication: Device PIN; on-device approval of policy registration, address display and signing.

interfaces.description: Bluetooth LE (Nano X, Nano Gen5, Flex, Stax), used by Ledger Wallet mobile; not used by HWI.
interfaces.authentication: Bluetooth pairing confirmed on the device.

cli: HWI: hwi enumerate (models ledger_nano_s, ledger_nano_x, ledger_nano_s_plus, ledger_stax, ledger_flex in 3.2.0; ledger_nano_gen5 only on master), hwi -t ledger -d <path> getxpub/getdescriptors/displayaddress/signtx. The Bitcoin app must be open on the device.
remoteManagement: None; local USB peripheral.
nodeCompatibility: Node-agnostic. HWI converts PSBTs to version 2 for the new app protocol and registers multisig wallets on the device during signing (requires the cosigners' xpubs in the PSBT global xpub field). Bitcoin Core can drive it through HWI as an external signer.

dependencies.notes: Ledger Wallet (formerly Ledger Live) installs and updates the Bitcoin app and Ledger OS.
Host software that exports xpubs, registers policies, displays addresses and signs PSBTs.

networking: None on the device; Bluetooth/NFC are local radio links.
security: Secure element (ST33K1M5, CC EAL6+ on the Nano S Plus; Nano X listed as EAL5+); Ledger OS is closed source, the Bitcoin app is open source. Ledger Recover (opt-in, identity-based subscription service provided by Coincover) splits encrypted seed entropy into three fragments held by Coincover, Ledger and EscrowTech (two needed for recovery); its 2023 announcement was controversial because it showed that the firmware can export seed material when the user consents. BTCortex must never promote or automate it. Incidents: Ledger Connect Kit npm supply-chain attack on 2023-12-14 (malicious versions 1.1.5-1.1.7 of a web library live for about five hours; Ledger says it did not affect devices or Ledger Live) and the e-commerce/marketing database breach of 2020-06-25 (about one million email addresses, 9 500 postal details), which keeps fuelling phishing. Bitcoin app hardening: 2.4.6 rejects miniscript policies with meaningless older(n); 2.5.0 requires a persistent setting to sign non-standard sighash flags. BTCortex: verify addresses on the device, store policy HMACs per wallet, never ask for the 24 words.
licenceNotes: Ledger OS is proprietary. The Bitcoin app (LedgerHQ/app-bitcoin) is Apache-2.0.
integrationMechanisms: Discover with hwi enumerate; show model (from the USB product ID), Bitcoin app version and fingerprint; ask the user to open the Bitcoin app if it is not running
Import xpubs/descriptors at standard BIP-44/49/84/86 and BIP-48/87 paths into watch-only wallets
Register multisig or miniscript policies on the device with explicit user approval and store the returned HMAC with the wallet
Display addresses on the device; sign PSBTs only after explicit user action
Launch Ledger Wallet for Ledger OS and Bitcoin app updates (close it before HWI sessions)

feasibility.notes: HWI supports all current models except the Nano Gen5 in the 3.2.0 release (the Gen5 product ID was added on master). The Bitcoin app is the most capable mainstream signer for policies: wsh and Taproot miniscript, multisig up to 15 cosigners (2.4.0), musig() key expressions (2.4.0). BIP-388 policy signing through HWI's signtx was merged on master on 2026-08-25 and is not yet released.

notes: The repository was renamed from LedgerHQ/app-bitcoin-new to LedgerHQ/app-bitcoin (the old URL redirects); the legacy app lives on as app-bitcoin-legacy. Unreleased changes on develop add BIP-322 message signing and make MuSig2 nonces independent of the transaction (only one pending signing session per policy). 'apex_p' is Ledger's build target name; HWI master maps product ID 0x80 to ledger_nano_gen5. Ledger announced a phone-like 'Ledger Atom' device on 2026-10-15 for reservation only (not verified beyond search results).

name: BitBox02 (BitBox02 and BitBox02 Nova, Multi and Bitcoin-only editions)
purpose: Swiss open-source hardware wallets from Shift Crypto with a dual-chip design (open firmware on a microcontroller plus a secure chip). They sign Bitcoin transactions after on-device confirmation and support multisig, miniscript wallet policies (including Taproot) and sending to silent-payment addresses.

platforms.windowsDistribution: No vendor driver (USB HID). The BitBoxApp (bitboxapp) performs firmware upgrades, including mandatory intermediate versions (9.17.1, 9.26.2). The device must be paired with a host once (Noise pairing code confirmed on the device); HWI driven by another program cannot show the pairing code and tells the user to pair in the BitBoxApp first and then close it.
platforms.other: USB-C on both models; the Nova adds Bluetooth LE (Whisper protocol on a separate DA14531 chip) used only by the BitBoxApp on iPhone/iPad; Windows, macOS, Linux and Android use USB. No QR or PSBT-on-microSD workflow.

interfaces.description: USB HID with a Noise-encrypted protobuf API; unencrypted device-info request returns firmware version, platform (BitBox02 or BitBox02 Nova), edition (Multi or Bitcoin-only), unlocked state and, since 9.27.1, the installed bootloader version. Attestation check proves the device is genuine.
interfaces.authentication: Device password entered on the device; host pairing (Noise) confirmed once per host.

interfaces.description: Bluetooth LE on the Nova, iOS BitBoxApp only.
interfaces.authentication: Whisper pairing.

cli: HWI: hwi enumerate (models bitbox02_multi, bitbox02_btconly, bitbox02_nova_multi, bitbox02_nova_btconly), hwi -t bitbox02 -d <path> getxpub/getdescriptors/displayaddress/signtx; multisig keys at m/48'/0'/<account'>/2' (p2wsh) or /1' (p2wsh-p2sh).
remoteManagement: None; local USB peripheral.
nodeCompatibility: Node-agnostic. The BitBoxApp uses Electrum servers; other wallets use the device through HWI or their own BitBox02 libraries.

dependencies.notes: Firmware upgrades, initial setup and first host pairing.
Host software for xpub export, policy/multisig registration and PSBT signing.

networking: None on the device.
security: Dual-chip design: secure chip ATECC608B on the BitBox02, Infineon Optiga Trust M V3 (EAL6+, NDA-free) on the Nova, which also enforces the 10-attempt password limit in hardware. Reproducible firmware builds with community signatures; the firmware hash shown at start-up is published per edition (9.27.1: Bitcoin-only 2522156c…bc73, Multi 38ddfd37…5648, Nova Bitcoin-only f48bb49f…acb4, Nova Multi d65b34fe…88fc). Security fixes: 9.15.0 fixed a fee attack reported by Saleem Rashid; 9.26.3 and 9.26.5 contain 'general security improvements'. Anti-klepto is required by BitBoxApp 4.52.0 for signing. BTCortex must only display, never relay, the pairing code, and must not attempt firmware flashing.
licenceNotes: Firmware licensed under Apache-2.0; BitBox is a trademark of Shift Crypto AG.
integrationMechanisms: Discover with hwi enumerate; show model, edition and firmware version; surface 'pair in the BitBoxApp, then close it' when HWI reports the device as unpaired
Import xpubs/descriptors (single-signature BIP-44/49/84/86, multisig BIP-48) into watch-only wallets
Register multisig script configurations or wallet policies on the device with explicit user confirmation
Display addresses on the device; sign PSBTs only after explicit user action
Launch the BitBoxApp for firmware upgrades

feasibility.notes: Fully supported by HWI 3.2.0 for both models and editions, with on-device multisig registration. Limits in HWI: no legacy (P2PKH) inputs and no P2SH (non-segwit) multisig; BIP-388 policy signing through HWI only on master (2026-08-25). The first host pairing needs the BitBoxApp.

notes: Feature history (CHANGELOG): 9.15.0 miniscript policies wsh(<miniscript>); 9.19.0 multisig at arbitrary keypaths; 9.21.0 Taproot policies, miniscript on Taproot and sending to BIP-352 silent-payment addresses; 9.27.1 message signing with keys in the m/48' namespace. HWI's published support matrix still marks BitBox02 Taproot inputs as unsupported, but hwilib/devices/bitbox02.py handles p2tr at m/86' (the matrix is outdated). The original BitBox02 cannot be upgraded to work with the iOS app.
unverifiedClaims: Whether the original BitBox02 (non-Nova) is still sold was not checked.
Dates of the 9.15.0, 9.19.0 and 9.21.0 feature releases were not recorded (the CHANGELOG has no dates).
Exact Windows behaviour when the BitBoxApp and HWI try to open the device at the same time was not tested.

name: Blockstream Jade
purpose: Open-source hardware signing devices from Blockstream (Jade Classic, Jade Plus and Jade Core) for Bitcoin and Liquid, connecting over USB serial, Bluetooth LE or air-gapped QR, with a blind-oracle PIN model, multisig registration and BIP-388 miniscript wallet policies.

maintenance.evidence: Firmware 1.0.41 dated 2026-08-22 in CHANGELOG.md ('important security updates; All users should upgrade as soon as possible'); 1.0.40 2026-04-30, 1.0.39 2026-03-06, 1.0.38 2025-11-26. Tags go up to 1.0.41; GitHub Releases are not used (firmware is served from jadefw.blockstream.com). Latest master commit 2026-10-16. Jade Core launched 2026-04-28; Blockstream's lineup post of 2026-06-02 lists Jade Classic, Jade Core and Jade Plus.

platforms.windowsDistribution: USB appears as a serial (COM) port, not HID. Blockstream's Windows troubleshooting offers two drivers when the device is not recognised: the WCH USB-serial driver and the Silicon Labs CP210x Universal Windows Driver; it does not say which model needs which. HWI recognises Silicon Labs (10c4:ea60), WCH (1a86:55d4, 1a86:7523), FTDI (0403:6001) and Espressif (303a:4001, 303a:1001) USB IDs. Only one application may hold the COM port at a time. QR mode needs a webcam on the PC; Bluetooth LE is used by the Blockstream app.
platforms.other: Hardware targets: jade (Jade 1.0, selection wheel), jade_v1_1 (Jade 1.1, rocker), jade_v2 (Jade Plus: larger screen, two buttons, camera, battery), jade_v2c (Jade Core: Jade Plus without camera and battery). Interfaces: USB-C serial, Bluetooth LE, camera QR (Classic and Plus), USB mass-storage host on ESP32-S3 models (PSBT files and firmware from an attached USB SD-card reader). DIY firmware for ESP32/ESP32-S3 boards such as M5Stack, TTGO T-Display, M5StickC Plus 2 and ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1. Companion apps: Blockstream app (desktop and mobile), Sparrow, Electrum, Specter Desktop, Nunchuk, Liana, BTCPay Server.

interfaces.description: CBOR RPC over USB serial (also over Bluetooth LE): get_version_info (JADE_VERSION, BOARD_TYPE, JADE_CONFIG, JADE_FEATURES, IDF_VERSION, EFUSEMAC, BATTERY_STATUS, JADE_STATE, JADE_INTERFACE, JADE_NETWORKS, JADE_HAS_PIN), auth_user, get_xpub, register_multisig (up to 16, COLDCARD-style multisig_file accepted), register_descriptor (up to 16 BIP-388 wallet policies, miniscript), get_receive_address, sign_psbt, sign_message, sign_attestation (ESP32-S3 units, RSA-4096) and OTA firmware update. HWI and the jadepy library use this interface.
interfaces.authentication: PIN entered on the device and validated by a blind PIN server; every signature is approved on the device. A wallet is held by one interface (SERIAL, BLE or QR) at a time.

interfaces.description: QR Mode (Bitcoin only, no Liquid): animated UR codes for PSBTs (crypto-psbt), account export (crypto-account or crypto-hdkey), raw bytes (for example multisig files), plus Jade-specific UR types for QR PIN unlock. Documented with Sparrow, Nunchuk and BlueWallet. QR PIN unlock lets the device reach the PIN server through a phone.
interfaces.authentication: PIN with QR PIN unlock, or a temporary 'Recovery Phrase Login' wallet.

interfaces.description: Bluetooth LE pairing with the Blockstream app (all current models).
interfaces.authentication: Device PIN and pairing.

interfaces.description: ESP32-S3 models (Jade Plus, Jade Core) can sign PSBT files and load firmware from attached USB storage such as an SD-card reader; a signed PSBT is written to a new file rather than overwriting the input.

cli: update_jade_fw.py (download the latest or a chosen --release, or flash a verified --fwfile, --serialport for the COM port) and jadepy with jade_cli.py from the firmware repository; HWI 3.2.0: hwi enumerate, then hwi -t jade getxpub, getdescriptors, displayaddress, signtx (native PSBT signing since 3.2.0) and signmessage. HWI master (unreleased, merged August 2026) adds registerdescriptor <name> <descriptor> and a --registration option for signtx and displayaddress (BIP-388 policies); 3.2.0 does not have them.
remoteManagement: None. The device is local. Firmware updates go through a companion app or update_jade_fw.py; metadata for each hardware type is published at https://jadefw.blockstream.com/bin/<jade|jade1.1|jade2.0>/index.json.
nodeCompatibility: Node-agnostic signer. The Blockstream app uses its own Electrum back ends or a user-configured server; Sparrow, Electrum (jade plugin in upstream Electrum), Specter Desktop, Nunchuk and Liana coordinate PSBTs against bitcoin-core or Electrum servers. Liana's timelocked recovery policies use register_descriptor (BIP-388 miniscript).

dependencies.notes: A companion or coordinator wallet builds PSBTs, relays PIN-server requests and broadcasts.
USB discovery, xpubs, descriptors, multisig/policy registration, address display and signing with on-device approval (Jade Plus support and native PSBT signing since HWI 3.2.0).
The PIN server has an onion address; routing the companion's PIN-server requests through Tor hides the user's IP address from Blockstream.

networking: Unlocking a PIN-protected wallet requires the companion to relay HTTP POST requests to the blind PIN server (default https://jadepin.blockstream.com/get_pin, onion alternative mrrxtq6tjpbnbm7vh5jt6mpjctn7ggyfy5wegvbeff3x7jrznqawlmid.onion); a self-hosted PIN server can be configured with update_pinserver. Without a network path the user must use 'Recovery Phrase Login' or 'QR PIN Unlock'. The device itself makes no network connections in normal use.
security: Blind-oracle PIN model: the PIN server cannot learn the PIN or keys but is needed to unlock; it sees the IP address of whoever relays the request unless Tor is used. Official units only run Blockstream-signed firmware installed through OTA; hashes (cmphash, fwhash) are published per hardware type in index.json and the fwhash is shown on the device before installation; builds are reproducible (REPRODUCIBLE.md). 1.0.41 (2026-08-22) is a security release: stack protection, a secure-version counter that blocks downgrades, extra per-device entropy for the initial seed and better memory scrubbing. Attestation (RSA-4096) on ESP32-S3 units and 'Genuine Check' on Jade Core. Wallets are locked to MAIN or TEST networks. DIY builds are unsigned unless the builder enables secure boot. BTCortex must never use Recovery Phrase Login, SeedQR or BIP-85 features on the user's behalf.
licenceNotes: Firmware is MIT-licensed; official units nevertheless only accept Blockstream-signed builds. BTCortex should not redistribute firmware.
integrationMechanisms: Detect over USB serial with HWI (hwi enumerate) and show model and fingerprint; get_version_info (via jadepy) exposes firmware version, board type, lock state and network lock without secrets
Retrieve xpubs and descriptors with HWI for a watch-only descriptor wallet in bitcoin-core or sparrow
Register multisig (COLDCARD-style multisig file) or BIP-388 policies, then confirm an address on the device (hwi displayaddress)
Sign PSBTs with explicit on-device approval through HWI, through UR animated QR (webcam) or via PSBT files on USB storage (Jade Plus/Core)
Route PIN-server traffic through Tor when the privacy profile is active, or document a self-hosted PIN server
Delegate device workflows to sparrow (preferred) or the Blockstream app

feasibility.notes: HWI supports Jade, including Jade Plus and native PSBT signing (3.2.0), and the RPC is documented. Windows-specific risks: USB-serial drivers on older units, COM-port contention with other wallets, PIN-server reachability (and its privacy) during unlock, and HWI's move to minimal maintenance.

notes: HWI device matrix, Jade column: xpub retrieval, message signing, P2PKH, P2SH-P2WPKH, P2WPKH, bare and P2SH/P2SH-P2WSH/P2WSH multisig inputs, arbitrary scriptPubKey/redeemScript/witnessScript inputs, non-wallet and mixed inputs, display on device; no setup, wipe, recovery or backup through software; Taproot inputs not marked as supported. Pricing per Blockstream (2026-06-02): Jade Classic $79, Jade Core $99, Jade Plus from $149. The 1.0.41 changelog adds Liquid descriptor registration on development devices only and a libjade desktop GUI example.

Blockstream help: compatible services with Jade
Blockstream blog: the Jade lineup reimagined (2026-06-02)

unverifiedClaims: Which USB-serial bridge each Jade revision uses (Silicon Labs CP210x or WCH CH9102/CH340) and whether Jade Plus and Jade Core (Espressif USB IDs) need any driver on Windows were not confirmed by Blockstream; the vendor-ID mapping is taken from HWI's device list.
Whether HWI 3.2.0 (released before Jade Core launched) recognises Jade Core (jade_v2c) was not tested.
Whether HWI's bundled Jade client honours a SOCKS proxy for PIN-server requests was not checked.
The exact UR types used for xpub export in QR mode depend on a user option (crypto-account or crypto-hdkey, per qrmode.c); the Sparrow guide was located by search, not read in full.

name: Foundation Passport
purpose: Bitcoin signing devices from Foundation: the air-gapped Passport Core (QR camera and microSD, no USB data; no longer produced but still updated) and its successor Passport Prime (KeyOS), which pairs with the Envoy mobile app over QuantumLink and works with desktop coordinators through QR codes and files.

maintenance.evidence: Passport Prime KeyOS 1.3.0 published 2026-07-17 (KeyOS 1.2.1 on 2026-04-14). Passport Core firmware v2.3.11 (release page dated 12 December; v2.3.11-beta-1 on 2025-12-02) with v2.4.0 betas adding miniscript (beta-1 2026-03-27, beta-2 2026-10-10, beta-3 2026-10-15). Foundation's glossary describes Passport Core as discontinued but still receiving firmware updates and documentation support.

platforms.windowsDistribution: No Windows driver. Passport Core exchanges data only through its camera (animated UR QR codes) and microSD; its USB-C port is power-only ('the data pins required are simply not present'). Desktop coordinators therefore need a webcam or a microSD reader. Passport Prime pairs with the mobile Envoy app over QuantumLink (Bluetooth) and uses QR codes or transaction files with other wallets; its USB 'Airlock' storage is read-only by default after disconnection.
platforms.other: Passport Core (including a Founder's Edition firmware build) and Passport Prime (KeyOS, a Rust operating system built on Xous, with apps such as Bitcoin Wallet, Files, 2FA, Security Keys, Vault and Legacy Mode). Companion: Envoy (mobile). Desktop coordinators documented by Foundation for Passport Core: Sparrow, Specter Desktop, Nunchuk and Keeper; also listed: Bitcoin Core, Bitcoin Safe, BlueWallet, Casa, Electrum, Fully Noded, Simple Bitcoin Wallet, Zeus; Bull Bitcoin connection flow added in 2.3.11.

interfaces.description: Animated UR 2.0 (Blockchain Commons) QR codes for account export, PSBTs and signed transactions; address verification by scanning a receive address. KeyOS 1.3.0 adds multisig configuration import via the crypto-output UR type (for Sparrow), single-part UR support and a universal QR scanner; Prime can export a multisig configuration (script type, threshold, co-signer xpubs) as a QR code or file.
interfaces.authentication: Device PIN; every signature is approved on the device.

interfaces.description: Passport Core microSD: PSBT files, wallet export files, multisig configuration files and firmware (.bin) updates; file hashes can be viewed on the device. Passport Prime: transaction files on external storage.
Passport Prime QuantumLink: encrypted Bluetooth link to Envoy for account sync, transactions and firmware updates (replay hardening in KeyOS 1.3.0).
interfaces.authentication: Pairing with Envoy

remoteManagement: None. Passport Prime firmware updates go through Envoy ('Update with Envoy'); manual updates are planned. Passport Core updates are .bin files on microSD.
nodeCompatibility: Node-agnostic signer; the coordinator (sparrow, specter-desktop, nunchuk, electrum, bitcoin-safe) talks to bitcoin-core or an Electrum server. No HWI support (Passport Core has no USB data path).

dependencies.notes: A coordinator builds PSBTs, shows them as QR codes or writes them to microSD, and broadcasts the signed result.

networking: None on Passport Core. Passport Prime communicates with Envoy over QuantumLink (Bluetooth); Envoy provides network access.
security: Passport Core only installs firmware signed by at least two Foundation team members (cosign tool); builds are reproducible by stripping the signatures from the release binary and comparing hashes; SHA-256 hashes are published in each release. KeyOS 1.3.0 (2026-07-17) followed a third-party audit (kernel, cryptography, USB, NFC, QuantumLink, PSBT handling) and fixed, among others, AES-GCM counter reuse in partial-block streaming, encrypted eMMC proceeding with all-zero keys, unauthenticated RemoteUpdate payloads, plaintext hot-wallet key material in logs, and validation of PSBT inputs against attacker-supplied funding data. Passport Core has no USB data path, which removes a host attack surface. BTCortex must not use Prime's seed import, Vault or BIP-85 features.
licenceNotes: Applies to the Passport Core firmware (passport2). The licence of KeyOS for Passport Prime was not verified; Foundation's developer page describes Prime's apps as open source in the KeyOS repository.
integrationMechanisms: Import a single-sig or multisig account from an animated UR QR code (webcam) or a microSD export file into a watch-only descriptor wallet

platforms.other: Keystone 3 Pro: 4-inch touchscreen, camera, fingerprint sensor, three secure elements, microSD, Shamir and passphrase support, $149. interfaces.description: FAT32 microSD: multisig wallet import (Sparrow 'Keystone Multisig' file), older PSBT workflows and firmware updates.

name: SeedSigner

maintenance.evidence: Release 0.8.7 ('The Summer of SeedSigner') published 2026-07-08 (release feed; manifest signature created 2026-07-07); 0.8.6 on 2025-06-30, 0.8.5 on 2025-02-04. dev branch commits on 2026-10-20. The release notes announce v0.9.0 and a microcontroller port in progress.

platforms.windowsDistribution: Nothing to install on Windows for signing: SeedSigner is QR-only, so the desktop coordinator needs a webcam that can read animated QR codes. Preparing the device on Windows means verifying the SeedSigner OS image (GPG and SHA-256) and writing it to a microSD card (64 MB or larger) with Balena Etcher or Raspberry Pi Imager.
platforms.other: Hardware: Raspberry Pi Zero v1.3 (recommended, no Wi-Fi or Bluetooth), Zero W and Zero 2 W, Pi 1, 2, 3, 4 and 400; Waveshare 1.3-inch 240x240 LCD HAT; OV5647 camera. Images seedsigner_os.<version>.pi0.img, pi02w.img, pi2.img and pi4.img.

interfaces.description: Animated UR QR codes for PSBTs in and out; BBQr PSBT decoding since 0.8.7; single-sig and multisig xpub export QR (format chosen directly since 0.8.7); SeedQR and CompactSeedQR for loading seeds; SettingsQR for configuration; scanning a coordinator's receive or change address to verify it; message signing.
interfaces.authentication: None stored on the device: the seed is entered or scanned each session and kept only in RAM. Every signature is approved on the device.

nodeCompatibility: Node-agnostic; compatible coordinators named by the project: Sparrow, Nunchuk, Keeper, BlueWallet and Specter Desktop, plus any wallet that supports QR PSBTs. Networks: mainnet, testnet and regtest.

dependencies.notes: A QR-capable coordinator builds PSBTs, shows them as animated QR codes and broadcasts the signed result.

networking: None: no Wi-Fi or Bluetooth on the Pi Zero v1.3; the microSD card can be removed after boot.
storage: microSD card of 64 MB or larger for the SeedSigner OS image (each image is under about 42 MB).
security: Stateless design: keys exist only in RAM and the SD card can be removed after boot so nothing can be written to it. Release images have been reproducible since 0.7.0 and are prepared and signed by 'SeedSigner the person'; the manifest seedsigner.<version>.sha256.txt is signed (.sig) with OpenPGP key 46739B74B56AD88F14B0882EC7EF709007260119 (Keybase user seedsigner; issuer confirmed from the 0.8.7 signature). integrationMechanisms: Import single-sig or multisig xpubs from the device's QR export into a watch-only descriptor wallet
Show PSBTs as animated UR QR codes (webcam on the device side) and scan the signed PSBT back after the user approves on the device; broadcast only after explicit confirmation
Show a receive or change address as a QR code so the device can verify it
Delegate device workflows to sparrow (preferred)
Link to the verified release images and verification instructions (do not flash on the user's behalf)

name: Krux
purpose: Open-source signing firmware for off-the-shelf Kendryte K210 devices (M5StickV, Maix Amigo and others) that signs PSBTs over QR codes or SD card and supports multisig, Taproot and wsh miniscript descriptors.

maintenance.evidence: v26.09.0 published 2026-10-03 (first release by the new maintainer jdlcdl, who took over from Odudex); 26.08.0 2026-08-04, 26.04.0 2026-04-27, 26.03.0 2026-03-26, 25.10.1 2025-10-30. The 26.09.0 notes say the K210 platform is discontinued by its manufacturer and that support for other microcontrollers needs community contributions.

platforms.windowsDistribution: Initial flashing from Windows uses Krux Installer (see krux-installer) or ktool over the board's USB serial (COM) port; later updates can be done from an SD card. Signing needs a webcam on the PC for animated QR codes or an SD card reader.
platforms.other: Supported boards (firmware packages): M5StickV, Maix Amigo, Maix Dock, Maix Cube, Maix Bit (not in every release), Yahboom k210, WonderMV, TZT CanMV (25.10.0), Embed Fire and WonderK PRO (26.03.0). Optional thermal printers for QR backups.

interfaces.description: Animated QR in UR (uppercase since 26.03.0; native uUR C module since 26.08.0), BBQr and pMofN formats for PSBTs, xpubs and wallet descriptors; loading a descriptor sets the wallet attributes (26.03.0).
interfaces.authentication: Mnemonic loaded per session (optionally from KEF-encrypted storage); every signature is approved on the device.

interfaces.description: SD card: PSBT signing that preserves all fields (so one file can be signed by several devices in turn), xpub text export, descriptor loading and firmware updates.
USB serial used only for flashing firmware (ktool or Krux Installer).

cli: ktool (ships in the release zip) flashes kboot.kfpkg for a device (m5stickv, amigo, cube, yahboom and others; on Windows the COM port may need to be given explicitly); `krux verify <zip> selfcustody.pem` or openssl pkeyutl verifies signatures.
nodeCompatibility: Node-agnostic. Coordinators named by the project: Sparrow, Specter Desktop, Liana and Bitcoin Safe (desktop); Nunchuk, BlueWallet and Bitcoin Keeper (mobile).

dependencies.notes: A coordinator builds PSBTs and exports the wallet descriptor for the device.
Desktop GUI for the initial firmware installation.

networking: None.
security: No secure element on K210 boards; mnemonics can be stored encrypted with the KEF format (AES modes including GCM). Advisories: 24.11.1 fixed AES-CBC encrypted mnemonics whose initialisation vector did not add the intended entropy; 26.09.0 fixed a 12-byte buffer overflow in GCM tag handling (assessed as non-critical, no user action needed). Releases: SHA256SUMS signed with the selfcustody ECDSA firmware key (.sig, DER, public key selfcustody.pem in the repository; the signature covers SHA256SUMS since 26.09.0) and with the maintainer's OpenPGP key (.asc; issuer 6DC76DC81B5C35D7F432712945D7F41053AF05F3 on the 26.09.0 signature); reproducible builds (firmware.bin, kboot.kfpkg, ktool) per ATTESTATION.txt. The project describes itself as research and development and requires acknowledging a disclaimer since 26.09.0. Hardware availability risk: K210 is discontinued.
licenceNotes: Krux code is MIT or Apache-2.0; the modified MaixPy firmware is Apache-2.0 with MicroPython/OpenMV parts under MIT.
integrationMechanisms: Import xpubs or a full descriptor exported by the device (QR or SD text file) into a watch-only descriptor wallet
Export the wallet descriptor (including miniscript) for loading on the device
PSBT round trip by animated QR (UR or BBQr) or SD card file; broadcast only after explicit confirmation
Delegate device workflows to sparrow, liana or bitcoin-safe
Offer krux-installer for initial flashing (external launcher)

feasibility.notes: Standard PSBT over UR/BBQr QR and SD files; DIY hardware on a discontinued chip family; best served through an existing coordinator.

notes: Multisig: P2WSH, P2SH-P2WSH (complete BIP-48) and legacy P2SH (BIP-45, 25.09.0); Taproot and wsh miniscript with indented visualisation since 25.03.0; non-standard sighash types are rejected before signing (26.04.0); PSBT fee checks hardened (26.08.0).

name: Specter DIY
purpose: Do-it-yourself Bitcoin signing device built from an STM32F469 Discovery board and a QR scanner, focused on multisig with Bitcoin Core-compatible descriptors and PSBTs; communicates over QR codes, USB or SD card.

maintenance.evidence: v1.10.5 published 2026-09-06 (maintenance release: RNG and change-detection hardening, embit 0.8.2, reproducible build fixes); v1.10.4 April 2026, v1.10.0 2026-01-29. Latest master commit 2026-10-07. Not stale.

platforms.windowsDistribution: QR mode needs nothing on the PC beyond the coordinator (the device has its own scanner and shows QR codes that the coordinator reads through a webcam). USB mode uses a plain-text serial protocol (Specter Desktop). Initial flashing is done over the board's mini-USB with the power jumper set to STLK; later upgrades come from an SD card and are verified by the secure bootloader.
platforms.other: STM32F469 Discovery board plus QR scanner and optional enclosures or shields; secret storage modes 'agnostic' (forget on power-off) and 'reckless' (stored in MCU flash); secure-element integration is announced as coming.

interfaces.description: Default host channel: unsigned PSBTs as base64 QR codes; the signed PSBT is shown as base64 with unnecessary fields stripped (only the global transaction and partial signatures), so the coordinator must keep and combine the original PSBT. Wallet descriptors (multisig, wsh miniscript) are imported by QR.
interfaces.authentication: PIN on the device; every signature is approved on the device.

interfaces.description: Plain-text USB serial commands terminated by \r or \r\n: fingerprint, xpub <derivation>, sign <psbt> (asks the user to confirm), wallet import and address verification.
interfaces.authentication: On-device confirmation.

interfaces.description: SD card: .psbt and .txt files processed like USB or QR input (transactions, wallet imports, address verification) and firmware upgrades (specter_upgrade_v<version>.bin).

nodeCompatibility: Designed for Bitcoin Core-compatible PSBTs and wallet descriptors, typically coordinated by specter-desktop; miniscript descriptors (wsh) are supported without policy compilation.

dependencies.notes: A coordinator builds PSBTs and keeps the original PSBT to combine with the stripped signed result.

networking: None.
security: Secure bootloader installed by the user (not at a factory) verifies two signatures on firmware upgrades; v1.10.3 rotated the bootloader signing keys, so devices on v1.9.0 or older must install v1.10.3 first. sha256.signed.txt is OpenPGP-signed by Mike Tolkachev, key F2DBC4C614C113E2B15F879ADD5C1264EBD645BE (issuer confirmed from the v1.10.5 signature); reproducible build signed by k9ert and Mike Tolkachev. v1.10.5 rejects dead TRNG output and requires verified descriptor derivation for change classification. No secure element: 'reckless' mode stores secrets in MCU flash.
integrationMechanisms: Import the device's xpub (QR, USB or SD) into a watch-only descriptor wallet
Export multisig or miniscript descriptors for import on the device
PSBT round trip by base64 QR or SD file; combine the stripped signed PSBT with the original; broadcast only after explicit confirmation
Delegate to specter-desktop or sparrow

feasibility.notes: Niche DIY hardware with its own QR conventions (plain base64 rather than UR) and a USB text protocol that only Specter Desktop implements; low demand relative to the effort.

notes: Release assets: specter_upgrade_v<version>.bin (upgrade via bootloader), initial_firmware_v<version>.bin (blank boards or firmware older than v1.4.0), sha256.signed.txt.

name: TAPSIGNER
purpose: Coinkite's battery-free NFC card that holds a BIP-32 key and signs transaction digests when tapped, used as a low-cost key in single-sig or multisig wallets (Nunchuk, Cove, Bitcoin Keeper, Sparrow).

maintenance.evidence: Offered for sale on tapsigner.com (2026-10-21); listed as supported by Nunchuk, Cove, Bitcoin Keeper and Sparrow; Coinkite's July 2026 COLDCARD advisory states TAPSIGNER is unaffected. The open protocol library coinkite-tap-protocol was last released as 1.2.2 on 2023-05-01.

platforms.windowsDistribution: Desktop use needs a USB CCID (PC/SC) contactless reader; Coinkite recommends the HID Omnikey CL5022 CL, which 'works well in Windows, Linux and MacOS'. Sparrow supports TAPSIGNER through a card reader. The cktap CLI needs Python with pyscard (SWIG may be needed to build it on Windows).
platforms.other: NFC card without screen or battery; phones (Android/iOS) through Nunchuk, Cove and Bitcoin Keeper; desktop through Sparrow.

interfaces.description: Coinkite's open NFC/APDU protocol (specification in coinkite-tap-proto): read the xpub for a derivation path, sign 32-byte digests, change PIN, export an AES-128-CTR encrypted backup of the master XPRV and derivation path.
interfaces.authentication: Card CVC/PIN (factory PIN must be changed before funding).

interfaces.description: cktap command-line tool (pip install 'coinkite-tap-protocol[cli]') for TAPSIGNER, SATSCARD and SATSCHIP.
interfaces.authentication: Card CVC/PIN

cli: cktap (coinkite-tap-protocol 1.2.2, Python, pyscard for PC/SC readers).
nodeCompatibility: Node-agnostic; the host wallet (sparrow on desktop) computes sighashes, assembles signatures and talks to bitcoin-core or an Electrum server.

dependencies.notes: The host wallet drives the card through a PC/SC reader (desktop) or phone NFC.

networking: None.
security: No screen or buttons: the card signs digests computed by the host, so transaction details cannot be verified on the device and the computer running the wallet must be trusted; Sparrow recommends cards for small to medium amounts. Backups are an encrypted file whose fixed 128-bit key is printed on the card, so the card plus the backup file recovers the wallet; there is no restore-to-card command. Not affected by the 2026 COLDCARD RNG incident. BTCortex must not drive TAPSIGNER signing itself (that would make BTCortex the transaction-verification point) and must never handle its backup or CVC.
licenceNotes: Card firmware is closed. The protocol library coinkite-tap-proto is published under the MIT licence text with the Commons Clause condition (COPYING-CC).
integrationMechanisms: Show compatibility and recommend sparrow with a PC/SC NFC reader
Import an xpub exported from the host wallet into a watch-only descriptor wallet
Detect PC/SC readers for diagnostics only (no card commands)

feasibility.notes: Direct integration would require BTCortex to compute and present sighashes as the only verification point, which conflicts with its non-custodial signing boundary; delegation to Sparrow is the safe path.

notes: Coinkite's related NFC cards SATSCARD (bearer card) and SATSCHIP are outside BTCortex's scope; Sparrow supports SATSCHIP through the same card API.

interfaces.authentication: Card PIN; optional second factor.

nodeCompatibility: Node-agnostic; the host wallet (sparrow) talks to bitcoin-core or an Electrum server.

dependencies.notes: Desktop host wallet with smartcard support (or Satochip's Electrum fork, not upstream electrum).

networking: None.
security: No screen: as with TAPSIGNER, the host computer must be trusted to show what is signed. v0.16-0.1 fixes a 2FA bypass in Musig2SignHash OP_FINALIZE and a non-compliant BIP-341 Taproot tweak found in code review, and adds point validation and constant-time MAC comparison; its API changes break older clients, which must be updated first. EAL6+ secure element per the vendor. BTCortex must not drive card signing or handle Seedkeeper secrets.
licenceNotes: Applies to the applet repository; other Satochip software repositories were not checked.
integrationMechanisms: Show compatibility and recommend sparrow with a PC/SC reader
Import an xpub exported from the host wallet into a watch-only descriptor wallet

feasibility.notes: Screenless card: safe use depends on a dedicated host wallet; BTCortex should only document the Sparrow path.

notes: The newest applet releases are marked pre-release; whether cards already sold can receive new applet versions was not checked.

The installer type, Authenticode signature and silent-install options of Satochip-Utils-win-amd64-0.4.0-beta-signed.exe were not checked.
The EAL6+ certification is a vendor claim that was not checked against a certificate.

name: Frostsnap
purpose: Distributed signing devices that use FROST threshold Schnorr signatures (Taproot) so that, for example, any two of three daisy-chained devices can sign for a wallet that looks single-sig on chain; coordinated by the Frostsnap app on Android, Windows, macOS and Linux.

maintenance.evidence: v0.4.0 published 2026-08-25 (security fixes), v0.3.0 August 2026, v0.2.x 2026; latest master commit 2026-10-20. Devices orderable at 150,000 sats each (frostsnap.com, 2026-10-21).

platforms.windowsDistribution: The coordinator app has a Windows x64 build: Frostsnap-v0.4.0.zip, the zipped Flutter release folder (portable, no installer; CI builds it on windows-latest). Each asset has a detached .asc signature and CHECKSUMS/CHECKSUMS.asc are provided, signed by the key 'Frostsnap <security@frostsnap.com>' (primary F19CCCCD876B6E57FB712206A9D5981F42B0EA50, signing subkey A0D99F559A2E20CFE6D18ABDFE2521845E568DAE). Devices connect over USB-C.
platforms.other: App: Android (APK/AAB), Linux AppImage, macOS DMG, Windows ZIP; no iOS. Device: ESP32-C3, 1.69-inch 240x280 touch display, two USB-C ports for daisy-chaining, aluminium case; Rust firmware (esp-hal).

interfaces.description: Devices connect to the app (and to each other in a daisy chain) over USB-C for key generation, signing and firmware upgrades.
interfaces.authentication: No device PIN; device secrets are encrypted with a key protected by the paired phone's secure element.

interfaces.description: Frostsnap app (Flutter) acting as FROST coordinator and wallet; uses Electrum servers for chain data.

nodeCompatibility: The app acts as the coordinator and uses Electrum servers (v0.4.0 notes mention Electrum error reporting and testnet/signet servers). FROST keys produce single-key Taproot outputs, so a watch-only import elsewhere would be a tr() descriptor; v0.4.0 adds descriptor checksum generation. Interoperability with sparrow or bitcoin-core watch-only wallets was not verified.

dependencies.notes: A self-hosted Electrum server could back the app; configuring it was not verified.

networking: The app connects to Electrum servers; devices have no network connection.
security: Threshold design removes the single point of failure of one device; keys are generated collaboratively with entropy from the phone or laptop. Devices have no PIN or secure element. v0.4.0 fixed a malicious-app attack that could get a device to sign an output hidden from its confirmation screen, and change addresses that could fall outside the recovery scan range; it also blocks firmware downgrades and publishes a deterministic firmware digest. FROST signing is not PSBT multisig: standard coordinators cannot co-sign, and recovery depends on Frostsnap's backup format. Young 0.x project without a published third-party audit.
integrationMechanisms: Download the Windows ZIP with its .asc, verify against the pinned Frostsnap key, extract per user and launch (external launcher)
Show compatibility information; watch-only import via a tr() descriptor only after interoperability is verified

feasibility.notes: Proprietary FROST coordination inside the Frostsnap app; no PSBT/HWI interoperability; immature (0.x).

notes: Distinct from PSBT multisig: on chain a FROST wallet is a single Taproot key, which improves privacy and fees but ties recovery to Frostsnap's tools.
unverifiedClaims: Whether the Windows app needs a USB driver for the ESP32-C3 devices was not checked.
Whether the app lets users choose their own Electrum server, and its configuration location on Windows, were not checked.
Watch-only export to Sparrow or Bitcoin Core was not verified.
The v0.3.0 and v0.2.x dates come from the release feed's 'updated' timestamps.

name: BHWI (Bitcoin Hardware Wallet Interface in Rust)
purpose: Work-in-progress sans-I/O Rust library from Wizardsardine (the Liana developers) for Bitcoin hardware wallets, with an async driver, a CLI and a Python-HWI-compatible 'hwi' binary; named by HWI's maintainer as a promising successor to HWI.

maintenance.evidence: Repository created 2024-07-04, last pushed 2026-10-19, description '[WIP] Bitcoin Hardware Wallet Interface in rust [WIP]'. Only a v0.1 tag and no GitHub releases on 2026-10-21. HWI issue #850 (2026-08-18) calls it 'a promising successor to this project'.

platforms.other: Rust crates for desktop, mobile, browser (WebAssembly via bhwi-wasm) and FFI callers; udev-rule installation is Linux only. Windows support is not documented.

interfaces.description: Sans-I/O device interpreters plus the bhwi-async driver (HID, USB serial, TCP, UDP, browser transports) for BitBox02, Coldcard, Jade, KeepKey, Ledger, Specter DIY and Trezor (Model One and Model T).
bhwi-cli provides a 'bhwi' command and a Python-HWI-compatible 'hwi' binary; a parity suite compares its output with Bitcoin Core HWI for the devices where parity is claimed.

cli: bhwi and an HWI-compatible hwi binary (built from source; no published binaries).
nodeCompatibility: Node-agnostic, like HWI.

dependencies.notes: Intended as a drop-in replacement for HWI's command-line interface.

security: Unreleased, work-in-progress code: not suitable for signing real funds until it has releases, signed artefacts and independent review. Capability gaps listed upstream: backup_device unsupported on several devices, register_wallet unsupported on KeepKey and Trezor, get_info unsupported on Specter DIY.
licenceNotes: Repository licence BSD-3-Clause (GitHub metadata); the BitBox02 integration carries a separate BITBOX_LICENSE file that was not reviewed.
integrationMechanisms: Track as the planned replacement behind BTCortex's signer adapter; evaluate its HWI-compatible binary against the same JSON contract once signed releases exist

feasibility.notes: No releases, no Windows binaries and no documented Windows support yet; the HWI-compatible CLI would make a later switch cheap if the JSON contract is honoured.

notes: A related Wizardsardine crate, async-hwi (used by Liana; 'The interface is not finalized ... specific to our needs with Liana'), has no tags or GitHub releases. Sparrow's Lark (Java) is the third HWI-derived library; it is embedded in Sparrow and has no releases of its own.
unverifiedClaims: Windows build and runtime support were not verified.
The claimed HWI output parity was not tested.

name: Trezor Bridge (standalone trezord-go)
purpose: Former standalone background service that let browsers and some third-party apps talk to Trezor devices through a local HTTP server; deprecated by Trezor in favour of the bridge built into Trezor Suite and WebUSB.

maintenance.evidence: Trezor's article 'Deprecation and removal of standalone Trezor Bridge' states that Trezor 'has deprecated the standalone Trezor Bridge' and that 'users are encouraged to uninstall the standalone Trezor Bridge' (page metadata; the article body was not retrievable on 2026-10-21). Last trezord-go release v2.0.33 (2023-04-17); repository not archived, last push 2025-04-14. Trezor Suite now runs its own JavaScript bridge (@trezor/transport-bridge) on 127.0.0.1:21328 and starts it when no external bridge is running.

platforms.windowsDistribution: Historically a Windows installer from data.trezor.io; the v2.0.33 GitHub release has no binary assets and current Windows artefacts were not checked.
platforms.other: Go source; Linux and macOS packages historically.

interfaces.description: HTTP server on http://localhost:21325 relaying Trezor wire-protocol messages; 'AJAX calls are only enabled from trezor.io subdomains' (README).
interfaces.authentication: Origin check only.

cli: trezord-go [-e/-ed emulator ports] [-u=false] (README examples).

dependencies.notes: Only useful with Trezor devices.
Suite starts its internal bridge only when no other bridge runs; a stale standalone Bridge interferes with current devices.

security: No longer updated by Trezor; keeping it installed means no security updates. HWI, Sparrow and Electrum do not need it (HWI talks HID/WebUSB directly). BTCortex should detect an installed or running standalone Bridge (service or process listening on 127.0.0.1:21325) and advise the user to uninstall it; it must never install it.
licenceNotes: COPYING contains the GNU LGPL version 3 ('-only' versus '-or-later' not checked).
integrationMechanisms: Diagnostics only: detect a listener on 127.0.0.1:21325 or an installed 'Trezor Bridge' entry and recommend uninstalling it

feasibility.notes: Deprecated by the vendor; superseded by Trezor Suite's built-in bridge and by direct WebUSB/HID access in HWI-based tools.

notes: Search results summarising the Trezor forum say the old Bridge cannot support the Safe 7's encrypted protocol (THP) and that older Model One devices on firmware 1.7.0 or below may not appear in Suite without it; these could not be fetched (HTTP 403/404).

sources.title: Deprecation and removal of standalone Trezor Bridge (page metadata)

unverifiedClaims: Statements that the standalone Bridge cannot support the Safe 7 encrypted protocol and the exact deprecation date come from forum posts that returned HTTP 403.
Whether trezor.io still serves a standalone Bridge installer for Windows was not checked.

maintenance.evidence: Repository archived by the owner on 2025-06-01 (read-only); last release v0.19.0 on 2023-06-02; README: Ledger Live (desktop) 2.44.0+ 'but don't go as far 2.53+ that breaks satstack'.

platforms.windowsDistribution: Last release ships satstack_0.19.0_Windows-amd64.zip, Windows-arm64.zip and Windows-arm.zip with a checksums file (2023).
platforms.other: Linux and FreeBSD archives (amd64, arm, arm64).

interfaces.description: Local explorer-compatible API consumed by Ledger Live (details not re-verified).

nodeCompatibility: Bitcoin Core RPC; not re-verified against Bitcoin Core 30+ (which removed legacy wallets and several import RPCs).

dependencies.notes: Only Ledger Live 2.44-2.52 per README.

security: Archived and unmaintained; incompatible with current Ledger Wallet versions. BTCortex must not install it.
licenceNotes: Not checked.

feasibility.notes: Archived; breaks with Ledger Live 2.53 and later. Use the Ledger device through Sparrow, Electrum or HWI with the managed node instead.
