name: BitBox01 (Digital Bitbox)
purpose: Shift Crypto's first, screenless hardware wallet (sold as Digital Bitbox); end-of-life.

maintenance.evidence: End of sale on 12 November 2019; Shift stopped actively releasing updates after November 2020; the 2FA relay server and mobile 2FA app were to be shut down by mid-2023 (blog post of 2023-01-18); the last BitBoxApp with full BitBox01 support is 4.37.3, later versions only manage backups.

platforms.other: USB.

interfaces.description: USB HID; HWI still ships a digitalbitbox driver (support matrix column 'BitBox01').
interfaces.authentication: Device password.

security: No screen: transaction and address details cannot be verified on the device (the smartphone 2FA verification service was shut down). End-of-life without updates. BTCortex should recommend moving funds to a supported signer and must not offer signing with it.
integrationMechanisms: Detection only (hwi enumerate) with an end-of-life warning

feasibility.notes: Screenless and end-of-life; signing without on-device verification is an unacceptable security risk for BTCortex.

notes: Recorded because HWI still lists it; users with funds on it need migration guidance, not integration.

sources.title: The end of the road for the BitBox01

unverifiedClaims: Whether the 2FA relay server was actually shut down in 2023 was not confirmed after the announcement.

name: Armory (Bitcoin Armory)
purpose: Long-running Bitcoin desktop wallet oriented towards cold storage (offline signing, paper backups) that indexes the chain with its own database (ArmoryDB) on top of a local Bitcoin Core node.

maintenance.evidence: Last stable release v0.96.5 on 2018-12-24. 0.97 RC1 was published on 2026-05-20 as a testing pre-release ('Do not expect something plug and play'; Windows ZIP only, mainnet untested by the author). Latest dev-branch commits 2026-05-20. Repository not archived.

platforms.windowsDistribution: 0.96.5: armory_0.96.5_win64.exe (installer) and armory_0.96.5_win64.zip, with sha256sum.txt.asc. 0.97 RC1 (pre-release): BitcoinArmory-0.97-RC1-win.zip (134 MB, mingw build on Windows 11; run ArmoryQt.exe) with sha256sum.txt.asc.
platforms.other: 0.96.5: Debian amd64 packages and a macOS tarball. 0.97 RC1: Linux from source only; no macOS build.

interfaces.description: ArmoryQt desktop GUI. 0.97 RC1 opens a settings manager with Wallets, Database and Core tabs (Core disabled) before the lobby.
interfaces.authentication: Wallet passphrase; 0.97 adds separate passwords for private and public wallet data.

interfaces.description: ArmoryDB database process; in 0.97 RC1 it can be automated or connected to a local or remote instance, with encrypted traffic in all modes.
Offline signing with unsigned and signed transaction files; 0.97 introduces a new .lmdb wallet format and a signer with a legacy mode for 0.96.5-era addresses.

remoteManagement: 0.97 RC1 can connect the GUI to a remote ArmoryDB instance over encrypted traffic.
nodeCompatibility: Needs a local, unpruned Bitcoin Core node: ArmoryDB reads the node's block data and relies on Core for networking. Bitcoin Core 28.0 and later XOR-obfuscate block files in new data directories (blocks\xor.dat), and older software cannot read a blocks directory with a non-zero key (see the full-nodes-core notes), so 0.96.5 is not expected to work with a fresh Core 28+ data directory; the dev branch merged a 'blockxor' change in May 2026, which suggests 0.97 handles it. Not usable with a pruned node (inference).

dependencies.notes: Local unpruned node; block-file obfuscation in Core 28+ is a known compatibility hazard for 0.96.5.

networking: Local connections to Bitcoin Core and ArmoryDB; 0.97 can use a remote ArmoryDB.
storage: 0.97 RC1 DB_BARE database: about 1 GB final size and about 20 minutes to build on the author's desktop (release notes); plus a full unpruned Bitcoin Core node.
resources: 0.97 RC1 DB_BARE: about 2 GB RAM at idle (release notes).
security: 0.96.5 is eight years old and predates current wallet standards (descriptors, Taproot, PSBT). 0.97 RC1 is explicitly a test build; its notes ask users to check the hash or signature before unzipping, but the signing key fingerprint is not published on the release page. Old wallets must be migrated (migration writes new files and leaves the old ones in place). Not suitable for BTCortex-driven installation.
licenceNotes: The README says Armory is 'distributed partially under the GNU Affero General Public License (AGPL v3) and the MIT License'; the exact split per component and whether 'only' or 'or later' applies were not checked.
integrationMechanisms: Detect an existing installation and show its status (stale stable line, test-only 0.97 RC) without configuring it

feasibility.notes: No stable release since 2018, a test-only 0.97 RC, block-file obfuscation incompatibility risks with current Bitcoin Core and no pruned-node support. P3; revisit if 0.97 becomes stable.

notes: The README lists 0.97 as the release target and says multi-signature support is about 80 % done. 0.97 RC1 known issues include Windows file operations hanging for up to a couple of minutes and a not-yet-optimised DB_FULL mode.
unverifiedClaims: Incompatibility of 0.96.5 with XOR-obfuscated Bitcoin Core 28+ block files is inferred, not tested.
That 0.97 RC1 supports obfuscated block files is inferred from a 'blockxor' merge on the dev branch.
The signing key behind sha256sum.txt.asc was not identified.
The architecture of the 0.97 RC1 Windows build is assumed to be x64 (mingw build on Windows 11).

name: Lily Wallet
purpose: Electron desktop multisig coordinator and wallet from Lily Technologies that builds multisig vaults from hardware wallets and reads chain data from the user's Electrum server; v1.3 added Lightning channel features.

maintenance.evidence: Latest release v1.4.0 on 2023-10-12 (v1.4.0-rc.1 2023-07-13, v1.3.0 2022-12-07). Latest commit 2023-08-14. The repository is not archived and has no discontinuation notice; the website still highlights v1.3 with a 2023 footer.

platforms.windowsDistribution: Lily.Wallet.Setup.1.4.0.exe (133 MB, Electron installer; architecture not stated). No signature or checksum files are attached to the release.
platforms.other: macOS arm64 .dmg and Linux AppImage; the repository also contains a Dockerfile, docker-compose files and an Umbrel-specific compose file.

interfaces.description: Electron desktop GUI for creating multisig vaults with hardware wallets (website lists Cobo Vault, Coldcard, Trezor, Ledger and BitBox02).
Retrieves blockchain data from the user's own Electrum server (README).

nodeCompatibility: Reads chain data from an Electrum server (unpruned node behind it). Its Bitcoin Core connection mode, if still present, was not verified against Bitcoin Core 30 or later.

dependencies.notes: Own Electrum server as data source.

networking: Outbound connections to the configured Electrum server; other services not researched.
security: No release since October 2023 and no commits since August 2023, so dependencies (Electron, hardware-wallet libraries) are unpatched for three years. Releases carry no signatures or checksums. Do not pre-configure or install it automatically.
licenceNotes: Elastic License 2.0 (README): not an OSI open-source licence; use, modification and redistribution are allowed but licence-key functionality must not be disabled or circumvented, and commercial use requires contacting the maintainers.
integrationMechanisms: Detect an existing installation and flag the project as stale

feasibility.notes: Stale for three years, unsigned releases and a source-available licence. Users should be pointed to maintained coordinators (sparrow, specter-desktop, nunchuk, bitcoin-safe). P3.

notes: Recent commits before the project went quiet touched Coldcard multisig export files and BitGo vault signing with Ledger.
unverifiedClaims: The Windows installer's architecture and Authenticode status were not checked.
Whether Lily still offers a direct Bitcoin Core connection, and whether it relied on legacy wallet RPCs removed in Core 30, was not verified.

name: Ashigaru Terminal
purpose: Terminal-user-interface (TUI) desktop wallet from the Ashigaru project, an independent continuation of Samourai Wallet's tools, used as a companion for Ashigaru Whirlpool (Zerolink) coinjoins: Tx0 creation and mixing or remixing from the Deposit, Premix, Postmix and Badbank accounts.

maintenance.evidence: Ashigaru Terminal v1.0.0 released 2025-06-23, the same day as the announcement of a new Zerolink coinjoin coordinator; Ashigaru Mobile v1.1.1 (Android) dated 2025-03-03 on the download page. No newer news post on 2026-10-21. The source repository is reachable only over Tor, so commit activity was not checked.

platforms.windowsDistribution: ashigaru_terminal_v1.0.0_windows.zip, downloadable only from an onion address (Tor Browser required). SHA-256 values are published on the clearnet download page inside a PGP-signed message; the key is published on Keybase ('ashigarudev') without a fingerprint on the site.
platforms.other: macOS x86_64 and aarch64 .dmg; Linux .tar.gz, .deb and .rpm; Ashigaru Mobile for Android.

interfaces.description: Terminal user interface usable on a desktop or a headless server; '-n testnet4' selects Testnet4 (mainnet by default). Configuration, wallets and logs in %APPDATA%\ashigaru.
interfaces.authentication: Wallet passphrase.

interfaces.description: Ashigaru Whirlpool coordinator (Zerolink coinjoins) and Dojo back end over Tor.

cli: Ashigaru-terminal executable; -n testnet4 starts on Testnet4. Other flags are not documented on the pages read.
remoteManagement: None documented; the TUI can run on a headless server over a terminal session.
nodeCompatibility: Back ends are not documented on the pages read; the project's documentation has wallet-server pages for Dojo. Compatibility with Bitcoin Core 30 and later was not verified.

dependencies.notes: Downloads and the code repository are Tor-only; coordinator and Dojo traffic run over Tor.

networking: Tor connections to the Ashigaru Whirlpool coordinator and the user's Dojo (details not documented on the pages read).
security: Legal context (neutral): Samourai Wallet's co-founders, whose Whirlpool design Ashigaru continues, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to operate an unlicensed money transmitting business and were sentenced in the US District Court for the Southern District of New York on 2025-11-06 (five years) and 2025-11-19 (four years); Samourai's coordinator and back-end servers were seized in April 2024. The Ashigaru developers are anonymous. Distribution is Tor-only and verification depends on a Keybase-hosted key without a published fingerprint, which BTCortex cannot pin. The project states it releases all code under GPL-3.0 and publishes a warrant canary.
licenceNotes: The website says all code is released under the GNU General Public License version 3; whether 'only' or 'or later' applies was not determined.
integrationMechanisms: Detect an existing installation (%APPDATA%\ashigaru) and show the project's status and legal context without installing or configuring it

feasibility.notes: Tor-only distribution, no pinnable signing-key fingerprint, undocumented back-end configuration and unclear maintenance after a single 2025 release; CoinJoin coordination also carries jurisdiction-dependent legal questions that BTCortex should not decide for the user. P3; the privacy-networking scope owns CoinJoin coordinators.

notes: Not to be confused with Microsoft's Windows Terminal. Whether Ashigaru Terminal derives from Sparrow Server is not stated on the pages read.

The Keybase key fingerprint, the Windows build's architecture and its runtime requirements (for example a bundled Java runtime) were not verified.
Commit activity in the Tor-only repository was not checked.

name: Whirlpool GUI (Samourai Wallet)
purpose: Discontinued desktop client for Samourai Wallet's Whirlpool CoinJoin, paired with the Samourai Wallet Android app and dependent on Samourai-operated coordinator and back-end servers.

maintenance.evidence: Samourai Wallet's founders were charged and arrested on 2024-04-24; the Whirlpool coordinator and back-end synchronisation servers were seized, so Whirlpool users of any client could no longer join coinjoins (NoBS Bitcoin, 2024-04-25). The founders were sentenced in November 2025 (SDNY). No releases since.

platforms.windowsDistribution: Historically an Electron desktop application; the official download host is no longer available and no artefact was verified.

interfaces.description: Desktop GUI that paired with Samourai Wallet and ran Whirlpool mixes through Samourai's coordinator (no longer reachable).

nodeCompatibility: Not applicable any more: the coordinator and back end it depended on were seized in April 2024.
networking: Historically Tor connections to Samourai's coordinator and back end; both are offline.
security: The software cannot function without the seized coordinator. Users with funds in old Samourai or Whirlpool wallets were advised to migrate them to another wallet such as Sparrow and to a new seed, because seized servers may hold their xpubs (NoBS Bitcoin). BTCortex should only detect it and show this guidance; it must never ask for the seed.
integrationMechanisms: Detect leftover installations and show a 'discontinued, cannot function' notice with a link to migration guidance in a maintained wallet

feasibility.notes: Its coordinator and back end were seized in 2024; nothing can be integrated. P3 detection-only record.

notes: Independent successors exist for parts of the Samourai stack (for example ashigaru-terminal); they are not official successors. CoinJoin coordinators are owned by the privacy-networking scope.
